Overall amazing experience., name_person=Sundeep Sikka}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=8 months ago, review=Restaurant/Food Review: Amadeo by Oberoi, Mumbai, India
Rating: 2/5

Wine Review:
Henri Bourgeois - Sancerre Les Baronnes 2022

A beautiful wine which is quite fruity and citrus which goes well with fish dishes.

Food Review:
I started with scallops dish as starter. It also had corn along with it.
It was tasty but a big failure.
It had too much stone like feel on mouth mostly because of burnt charcoal/carbon in corn.
This was not expected from such a restaurant.

Followed by a Japanese style tempura fried prawns and rice rolled like a sushi.
The basic problem with the dish was it was deep fried and also was giving too much of tamarind flavour.
It was not great I would say having tried some real Japanese sushi in some other restaurants.

Next, I tried spaghetti with crab which was quite average as well.

What I understood is the Chef is concentrating on more fried dishes which gives great taste, but very bad for health.
Indians would certainly love fried dishes, but any European/American/Australian person would never even eat such food as it’s unhealthy.

In my opinion, the restaurant failed to reach even fine food status.
Chef needs to improve a lot.

Quality food and flavors.
Perfectly portion controlled to comply with healthy lifestyle, individual portions perfect for one person.
Set menus aren’t recommended for sharing.

If you decide to do the set menu, all the guests on the table must do a set menu.

Loved the Italian.

[{'name_person': 'J S', 'time_line': '2 weeks ago', 'review': 'The place promises a lot but fails to deliver. Be it the ambience or the food.

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)

Tamnak Thai in Dadar Shivaji Park, Mumbai, has solidified its place as my absolute favorite Thai restaurant after multiple delightful visits, with my latest being on September 1, 2025. Nestled on Veer Savarkar Marg opposite Starbucks, this spot offers an authentic Thai escape with its warm, oriental ambiance—think elegant sculptures, soft lighting, and spacious seating that feels like a trip to Bangkok. The staff, including our attentive server who expertly guided us through the menu, delivered courteous and efficient service, enhancing the cozy in-house experience at Table No. 5. The absence of a service charge is a thoughtful bonus in Mumbai’s dining scene.
Our meal began with refreshing drinks that set the tone perfectly. The Cinderella mocktail (₹460) was a delightful blend of tropical fruitiness with a fizzy twist—light, sweet, and utterly refreshing. Paired with it, the Himalayan mineral water (₹140 per bottle, 2 bottles at ₹280 total) offered a crisp, pure hydration that complemented the flavors ahead. The Iced Tea (₹240) brought a chilled, subtly sweet note, while the Kiwi Kooler (₹460) burst with fresh kiwi and a tropical fizz, and the Virgin Mojito (₹460) delivered a classic minty-lime zing—each generously portioned and served promptly.
For appetizers, the Phad Khi-Mao Kung (stir-fried prawns with basil and chilies, ₹1040) was a spicy masterpiece, with juicy prawns and holy basil creating a bold, aromatic dish. The Satay Kai (chicken satay skewers, ₹860) featured tender, perfectly grilled meat with a creamy peanut sauce that balanced sweet and spicy notes flawlessly. Mains were a highlight, starting with the Tom Yam Kai (chicken Tom Yum soup, ₹520) and Tom Yam Kung (prawn version, ₹560), both tart and fragrant with lemongrass and chilies, warming us up delightfully. Pla Rad Phrik (fish in chili sauce, 2 portions at ₹980 each) offered crispy fillets in a tangy chili-garlic glaze, while Kaeang Phed Kai (red chicken curry, ₹780) was rich with coconut milk and tender chicken, paired with aromatic Khao Hom Mali (sticky rice, ₹380). The Koi Tiow Phad Thai Kai (Pad Thai noodles with chicken, ₹560) rounded it off with its sweet-tangy tamarind sauce and wide rice noodles, every dish arriving hot and fresh.

The total gross amount was ₹9120 before taxes, with CGST and SGST at 2.5% each (₹228 apiece), bringing the bill to around ₹9576—a fair price for the quality and authenticity. The fresh ingredients and genuine Thai flavors, honed over visits, make the cost worthwhile.

Tamnak Thai consistently delivers an explosive taste experience, seamless service, and a relaxing vibe. It’s my go-to for Thai cuisine in Mumbai, and I can’t wait to return. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Recently, I visited Hitchki located in Powai, and it turned out to be a wonderful dining experience. The ambiance of the place was so beautiful and amazing, with a lively vibe and stylish décor that made the visit even more special. The seating arrangement was comfortable, and the overall atmosphere was perfect for friends, family gatherings, and celebrations.

We began our evening with cocktails, and they were truly impressive. Boot E Licious was refreshing with a great balance of flavors, while Talli Main Talli Hogayi was fun, unique, and definitely lived up to its name. Both drinks set a great start to our meal.

In starters, we ordered Butter Chicken Seekh Kebab, which was soft, perfectly spiced, and delicious. Along with that, we had Prawn Jaye Par (butter garlic prawns), which were juicy, flavourful, and simply outstanding—the aroma of butter and garlic made it irresistible.

For the main course, we enjoyed Saoji Mutton with butter roti. The mutton gravy was rich, spicy, and full of authentic flavors, and the meat was tender and well-cooked. We also had Chicken Tikka Biryani, which was fragrant, aromatic, and packed with amazing taste. The combination made the meal very satisfying.

To end on a sweet note, we had Kalakand Shahi Tukda Roll. It was beautifully presented and tasted heavenly, with the perfect balance of sweetness and texture.

["{guided_block={}, time_line=a month ago, review=I visited Hitchki BKC and had such a wonderful experience.
Ryan, our steward, was extremely attentive and made sure we tried the best dishes.
We started with NARANGI, a nostalgic orange candy drink with a lemony twist – so refreshing.
The He-Man mocktail with Red Bull, orange juice, peach, and grenadine was energising and tasty.
Malay Fish Tikka came tandoor-smoked with Malaysian spices and coconut curry flavours – absolutely delicious.
The Prawn Jaye Par… had perfect butter garlic flavour with a nice hint of parmesan and orange zest.
Their Chicken Tikka Pressure Cooker Biryani was a showstopper, served whistling on the table, packed with herbs, kaju, kismish and amazing aroma.

The restaurant has an outdoor and indoor seating section and there's a small roof top section which I didn't explore. The ambiance of the place closely matches the Mexican vibes while it can seat people of all group sizes. At the very end of my meal, i saw they had kept board games as well! While the music playing in the background had good selection of western songs and not something the ones popularly played on Instagram reels these days, which is the case with certain restaurants.

The staff experience is good. Viraj was the one who assisted for the night, he was good at explaining the menu as well as mocktails. The dishes were handed out in a timely manner and nothing felt rushed.

[{'name_person': 'dhawal gala', 'time_line': 'a month ago', 'review': 'I recently visited **Amaari in Malad**, and honestly, it turned out to be one of those places that leaves you genuinely impressed—not just because of the food, but the complete experience. From the moment you walk in, you can feel that the restaurant has put real thought into creating a warm, welcoming vibe. The ambience is classy yet comfortable, with beautiful lighting, well-spaced seating, and a calm atmosphere that works perfectly whether you’re going with family, friends, or even for a relaxed date.

One of the best parts about Amaari is how balanced the overall setting feels. It’s not overly loud, not too formal, and not the kind of place that feels rushed. The interiors are tastefully done, clean, and elegant, and everything from the music to the seating arrangement adds to the comfort. It’s the kind of restaurant where you can actually sit, talk, enjoy your meal, and take your time without feeling like you need to leave quickly.

Coming to the food—Amaari definitely delivers. The quality and presentation of the dishes were excellent, and you can tell the ingredients are fresh. Every dish we tried had great flavour, and what I liked most was that the food wasn’t overly oily or heavy. The taste felt well-balanced, which is rare in many places. The portions were also quite satisfying, and the plating was very appealing.

The menu has a good variety, and whether you’re someone who likes classic comfort dishes or you enjoy trying something slightly different, there’s enough to choose from. The flavours were consistent, and each dish felt thoughtfully prepared rather than rushed. Even the small details like the dips, accompaniments, and seasoning were on point, which shows the kitchen really cares about what they serve.

Now, the service deserves a special mention. The staff was polite, attentive, and well-mannered throughout. They guided us properly with suggestions, explained items when we asked, and made sure everything was served on time. What I appreciated the most was that they were present when needed but never intrusive. You don’t always get that balance, but Amaari’s team handled it perfectly. The overall hospitality was warm, and it genuinely enhanced the dining experience.

Another thing worth appreciating is the cleanliness and overall maintenance of the place. The restaurant felt hygienic and well-managed, and even during busy hours, the service and quality didn’t drop. That’s always a big plus.

Overall, **Amaari in Malad** is a restaurant I would happily recommend to anyone looking for a place with **good ambience, delicious food, and excellent service**. It’s not just about eating here—it feels like a complete dining experience. I’ll definitely be visiting again, and it’s the kind of place that deserves to be on your “go-to” list if you enjoy good food in a beautiful setting.', 'guided_block': {'GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT': 5, 'GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT': 5, 'GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT': 5}}, {'name_person': 'Arun S.', 'time_line': 'a month ago', 'review': '**Amaari – Link Road, Malad West**

The place also works well as a semi-banquet with music and disco lights for celebrations.

**Starters**
• *Kung Pao Paneer* – Soft paneer tossed in a flavourful kung pao sauce, a perfect Indo-Chinese starter.
• *Paneer Pizza* – Loaded with paneer and cheese, filling and satisfying.

**Mains**
• *Paneer Lababdar with Butter Naan* – Rich, creamy and a great choice for Punjabi food lovers.
• *Veg Biryani* – Aromatic and flavourful, topped with cashews and caramelised onions, generous portion size.

**Dessert**
• *Brownie with Vanilla Ice Cream* – Warm, chocolaty and comforting.

**Drink**
• *Whiskey Riskhey* – A smoky, cinnamon-infused chilled drink with a unique twist.

**Overall:** Good food, family-friendly ambience, value-for-money weekday offers, and a perfect place for small celebrations or corporate parties.

Loved their refreshing mocktails 🍹 and the Veggie Gardenia Pizza 🍕—flavourful and perfectly baked.
The spring rolls were super crispy 🤤 and the Mexican nachos had a great taste.

When dining at The Brasserie, located inside the Hilton at Mumbai International Airport, you’re greeted with a mix of first impressions, starting from the entry itself. The entrance to the hotel can feel a bit cramped, with space limited to accommodate just 2-3 cars at a time on the flat surface, combined with a steep slope for both entry and exit. While valet parking is available, the service felt slightly understaffed, with seemingly only one person managing both the boom barrier and valet parking.

Once past security, you’re welcomed into a cozy and elegant Hilton lobby. Although it’s not grandiose in size, its beauty lies in its thoughtful design. The elegant couches and a glossy white grand piano create a subtle yet refined atmosphere, making it an inviting space. To the left of the lobby is The Brasserie, where we had a lunch buffet.

Ambiance:
The restaurant itself is on the smaller side, accommodating about 50 people. Despite its compact size, the restaurant wasn’t crowded when we arrived for our 2 pm reservation on a Saturday. The place was 80% empty, offering a calm and quiet environment. However, the overall ambiance didn’t exude the level of luxury you might expect from a Hilton property. The seating arrangements were functional but could have been more comfortable, particularly if you’re expecting a more lavish dining experience.

Food:
The buffet featured a wide variety of options, with both vegetarian and non-vegetarian selections available. The spread included:

•	Soups: 1 veg and 1 non-veg option.
•	Salads: 9 different varieties.
•	Starters: 4 options (2 veg, 2 non-veg).
•	Main Course: A mix of Indian and Chinese cuisine, with 4 gravies (2 veg, 2 non-veg), rice, noodles, and a few Chinese gravy dishes.
•	Rice options: Chicken Biryani, Dal Tadka, and Jeera Rice.
•	Non-Veg: Chicken, fish, and egg preparations.
•	Live Counters: Pizza, pasta, and a choice of breads (roti, naan, etc.).
•	Desserts: A decent variety with fruits, pastries, mousse shots, Indian sweets (Barfi, Malai Sandwich), ice creams, and a hot melted chocolate brownie alongside malpuva.

The quality of food was excellent, earning a solid 5/5. Every dish tasted fresh and well-prepared, although the overall taste ranked slightly lower at 4/5, as a few dishes didn’t fully hit the mark in terms of flavor depth. Still, with the wide variety on offer, there was something for every palate.

Service:
The service was decent, but could have been better. With only a few tables occupied, you’d expect more attentiveness from the staff. While they were polite and quick to respond to requests, the overall experience felt a bit lacking in terms of personalized service. For a property under the Hilton name, the expectation of seamless, luxurious service was not fully met, leading to a score of 4/5.

Cleanliness and Ambiance:
The restaurant was clean and tidy, giving off a neat and well-maintained vibe. However, the ambiance didn’t quite match the luxury you’d expect from a high-end hotel dining experience. It was pleasant but lacked a certain “wow” factor that you might anticipate at this price point. This led to a score of 3/5 for both the feel of luxury and sitting arrangements, as these could have been more comfortable and plush.

Overall:
For INR 3,221 per person, including taxes, the buffet at The Brasserie offers decent value if you’re looking for a variety of food in a quiet, elegant setting. The food quality is top-notch, and there’s enough variety to satisfy most diners. However, the experience could be enhanced with a more luxurious ambiance, better seating arrangements, and more personalized service.

•	Cleanliness: 4/5

Caspers Bar and Kitchen is one of those places you keep coming back to once you’ve been there. The ambience is really well done—it strikes the perfect balance between modern and cozy. Whether you're out with friends for drinks, on a casual date, or just in the mood for a relaxed dinner, Caspers delivers on all fronts.

The food menu is quite extensive with plenty of options across Indian, Chinese, and Continental cuisines. I’ve tried their starters, sizzlers, and pizzas, and everything was well-prepared and served hot. Their paneer dishes and chicken platters especially stand out—flavorful, juicy, and perfectly spiced. The bar menu also has a good selection of cocktails, mocktails, beers, and spirits at reasonable rates.

Service is another big plus. The staff is friendly, attentive, and quick to respond. The seating is comfortable, music is at the right volume, and the overall vibe makes you want to stay longer.

reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=Edited 7 years ago, review=Sofitel Wine Days are back! This is held on a monthly basis at The Sofitel Mumbai BKC and I was lucky to be a part of one at Le Bar Diamantaire, located at lobbey level next to Pondicherry Cafe!

A sit down multi course Italian meal with Italian wine is what you witness! An experience unparalleled. Sofitel has always been my one of the most favourite places in Mumbai because of the numerous festivals they do. But the food tried at this event was one of the best that I have ever had!

Every course had its own wine, started with couple of white and finishing with couple of red! All the wines had been specially curated and imported and the food also complemented really well. You have Veg as well as Non Veg options, so one can choose accordingly. Talking about what all I tried at Sofitel Wine Days -

We began with Almond and Goat Cheese as Starters, had Zucchini, Avocado and Mustard Sauce. The non veg equivalent to this was Amaranth Prawns. This was served with the first wine of the evening - Villa Antinori Bianco - white wine. A perfect way to begin your meal! The wine aims at maximizing the Tuscan character of the wine and is straw yellow in colour with greenish highlights. It is still wine with approx 12% alcohol by volume.

Next in line we tried the Forest Mushroom Veloute which was Truffle Mousse, Pine nuts and brioche. Absolutely awesome and I loved the taste! Texture was thick and rich in flavour and aroma. This was served with the second white wine of the evening - Antinori Santa Cristina Pinot Grigio. The wine is straw yellow in colour, the wine offers fruity and delicate aromas of pineapple, green apples and lemon. The wine is refreshing and has approx 12% alcohol by volume.

Moving to the mains - we first had the Baked Courgette which was Duxelle, Edamame and Parmesan Risotto! Again an awesome dish for Mushroom lovers. This was served along with the first red wine of the evening - Antinori Santa Cristina Toscana. For non vegetarians there was Grilled Seabass (Risotto). Wine is a red wine from Toscana, Italy and has approx 12.5% alcohol by volume.

Next main dish was Grilled Polenta which had red lentil ragout, charred leek, fondant potato and caramlised onion straw! A filling dish and really good! I preferred Polenta more than Baked Courgette! This one was served along with Antinori Peppoli Chianti Classico, the last wine / 2nd red wine of the evening. Non veg equivalent was Braised Lamb Shank with same ingredients. The wine represents the Chianti Classico territory and it's historic grape variety with typical floral and fruity aromas. Wine has approx 13% alcohol by volume.

We ended our meal with one of the most amazing desserts - Berry Trail. It had Raspberry Parfait, Blueberry Jelly, Blackberry Chantilly, Oats Crumble and Berry Chocolate Crisps. One of the best dessert that I have had till date! Simply awesome.

In complete awe of the experience at Sofitel Mumbai BKC! As mentioned earlier, they keep doing #sofitelwinedays often, almost every month and I would highly recommend everyone including all wine connoisseurs!, name_person=Jatin Shah}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=Sofitel BKC  has been our favourite hub to enjoy some family times , thanks to their Festivals which they organise with great enthusiasm .

This time it was our time to be a part of their Italian Fiesta Festival at Le Bar Diamantaire which was in collaboration with Ferrari Mumbai .

Le Bar has a Classy Ambience and flaunts to be one of the rare restaurant in Mumbai having a Wine Tower of its own . What will amaze you more is the food they serve which is just too good to be missed .

Lastly Not to Forget the Red Beauty ie Ferrari standing at the door step of the Sofitel.

Let's straight move on to what all we savoured out here during our visit .

Appetizers :

Bruschetta :
An amazing start to a classy evening . Crisp bread with luscious Topping ....

Arracini Balls :
Hot balls having a Scrummy peas based stuffing .

Polenta :
Boiled Cornmeal served with a tasty mushrooms preparation served along side .

Mains :

Cannelloni :
An immaculately presented dish with spinach Cannelloni served with Salsa Rosa . This a definite must to enjoy delicacy of the outlet .

Lasagna :
Again a super delicious dish straight from the treasure box of chef special delicacy of the outlet .

Mocktails :

We went for our all time favourite classic Mocktails during our visit . Mojito ,  Shikanji and Blue Curacao were amongst the Favourites .

Dessert:

Tiramisu :
After a very long time we really enjoyed our most beloved dessert at this super cool place .

Zucotto :
Now that's a dessert for which we will visit the place soon again . Just don't miss on this the moment you are going for dessert out here . Outer coating of chocolate Creamy pastry stuffed with freezing cold icecream and fruits .

Do visit the Italian  Food Fiesta  at Le Bar Diamantaire  Sofitel  before 21st  June  2018 to have a great experience as we did.

reviews: ["{\"name_person\":\"WheelsAndSpoons\",\"time_line\":\"3 weeks ago\",\"review\":\"**Dining at Amelia, BKC feels less like visiting a restaurant and more like stepping into a curated world\u2014one where elegance isn\u2019t performed, it\u2019s lived.**\\n\\nFrom the moment you walk in, the room greets you with a warm golden glow. The atmosphere is a blend of chic minimalism and soft eccentricity\u2014velvet textures, polished marble, muted tones, and a gentle hum of conversations that feel like they belong to a cosmopolitan private club. Amelia doesn\u2019t try to impress you loudly\u2026 it seduces you slowly.\\n\\n**The experience begins with the service**\u2014attentive without hovering, knowledgeable without overwhelming. Every recommendation feels personal, like a quiet nudge from someone who genuinely wants you to taste their favourites.\\n\\n**Then comes the food\u2014artful, refined, and quietly dramatic.**\\nDishes arrive like small performances: plating that\u2019s thoughtful, flavours that layer themselves gradually, and ingredients that feel global but grounded. Whether it\u2019s the buttery tenderness of their signature mains, the delicate acidity in their seafood dishes, or the rich, indulgent desserts that close the evening, every bite feels curated with intention.\\n\\n**Cocktails at Amelia deserve their own chapter.**\\nCrafted with precision, they balance experimental notes with classic elegance\u2014the kind of drinks that elevate a conversation and slow down time.\\n\\nWhat makes Amelia special is its **energy**. It\u2019s sophisticated without snobbery, luxurious without noise. Perfect for date nights that need a touch of magic, celebrations that deserve good taste, or evenings when you just want to feel a little bougie.\\n\\nYou don\u2019t just dine at Amelia, BKC\u2014you *experience* it.\\nA place where ambience, flavour, and finesse come together so seamlessly you\u2019ll find yourself planning your next visit before you even step out\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Lunch\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,600\u20131,800\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Shaikh Khalid Sarfaraz\",\"time_line\":\"3 weeks ago\",\"review\":\"Amelia is located in BKC One and it is easy to find.\\n\\nThe restaurant is decent in size with perfectly placed bar. The decor is minimal yet it looks extremely elegant and royal. The lightings, the seatings, the walls and every corner of this restaurant looks beautiful. The moment you enter it definitely gives a special feeling.\\n\\nThey specialise in authentic Italian cuisine and hence the menu is perfectly curated. Loved the menu as it covers a lot of variety hence options are great for both vegetarians and non vegetarians. Prices are at par with similar type of brands and the quantity served is good.\\n\\nWe went here for their special Sunday brunch for which they have a different menu. To our surprise there was live violinist which was excellent. The kitchen service was on time and table service by staff Uzair was good. Special thanks to Chef Ravish who was very humble and he suggested perfect dishes as per our liking.\\n\\nWhat We Had -\\nAPPETISERS~\\nSmoke & Spice Flatbread -\\nPerfectly done flatbread topped with bell peppers, jalape\u00f1os, shredded chicken and cheese. Loved the taste of this as the fresh jalape\u00f1os tasted really good and their tomato sauce wasn\u2019t tangy.\\n\\nWild Mushroom Symphony -\\nA treat for mushroom lovers. Earthy mushroom sauce with truffle oil topped with sunny side up egg tasted heavenly. Loved every bit of this as it was very flavourful and the crunchy fried mushrooms on the top with light parmesan cheese added perfectness to it. A must try.\\n\\nHarissa Gambas Cube -\\nSoft bread filled with creamy sauce and loads of fresh prawns tasted great. Loved the sauce as it wasn\u2019t too spicy and the prawns went perfectly with the sauce. The bread again was not too much hence everything was just right in this dish.\\n\\nMAINS~\\nBurrata & Truffle Ravioli -\\nRavioli filled with burrata cheese topped with butter sauce, almonds and garlic tasted delicious. Loved the thin layering of the ravioli and the cheese inside was excellent. The butter sauce was not salty as almonds and garlic balanced the taste. Loved eating this.\\n\\nChicken Scallopini -\\nGrilled chicken with saut\u00e9ed veggies done in lemon butter sauce tasted good. Loved the chicken as it was juicy and tender plus the sauce wasn\u2019t too salty and had perfect flavours.\\n\\nDESSERT~\\nRaspberry Tres Leches Royale -\\nChef Ravish told us to try this as personally I don\u2019t like berry based desserts and to my surprise this was outside. reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=We recently visited Yazu, Andheri, and it completely impressed us with its amazing Pan-Asian experience. The ambience is subtle yet classy, with dim lights and soothing vibes — a perfect spot for a relaxed dinner with friends or loved ones.

For drinks, we tried the Mock Penzi and Strawberry & Orange Mojito. Both were beautifully presented with a slightly sweet note — refreshing and perfect to kickstart the meal.

Coming to the starters, the Yazu Signature Chicken was an absolute treat — a perfect balance of sweet and spicy, topped with cashews and onions for that added crunch. Next, we tried the Pan-fried Chicken Shanghai Dimsums, which were flavourful and well-cooked. The Manchow Soup was comforting, rich in taste, and just perfect for the winter season.

The highlight of the evening was definitely the Crispy Prawns Cheng Fung — a must-try dish here! For mains, we opted for the Burnt Garlic Fried Rice, which had subtle yet delicious flavours and paired well with the rest of the spread.

We wrapped up our meal with the Pick Me Up Tiramisu Cake, which was decadent and delightful — a perfect ending to a perfect meal.

Special mention to Mr. Suraj for suggesting some amazing dishes and enhancing our overall dining experience.
Yazu is a must-visit place for all Asian food lovers! Highly recommended. 🌟, name_person=priyanka shikhare}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Yazu brings a refreshing Pan-Asian twist to the Unlimited Buffet Brunch scene in Andheri. The ambience is warm, stylish and perfect for a relaxed yet indulgent Sunday outing. 🥂🍜

The brunch menu offers a well-curated variety of Asian favourites—enough to tempt every palate without feeling overwhelming. You get comforting soups like Manchow & Tibetan Thenthuk, flavour-packed salads, a delicious range of dimsums such as Truffle Edamame, Cream Cheese & Sriracha Chicken Dumplings, along with assorted sushi rolls and wok starters including Spicy Cottage Cheese, Signature Chicken & Black Pepper Fish.

The main course keeps it soulful with classics like Thai Green Curry, Black Bean Chicken, Fish in Chilli Basil, Veg Fried Rice, Hakka Noodles & more. The best part? You can savour it all as part of the unlimited brunch — making it value-for-money if you love exploring multiple flavours in one meal.

A great pick for a premium yet comforting Sunday brunch with friends or family — good food, soothing ambience and a menu that truly celebrates Pan-Asian cuisine. 🌿✨, name_person=Purva Sangade}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=Tucked away right behind Infinity Mall in Lokhandwala, Andheri West, Yazu The Pan Asian Supper Club is truly a paradise for Asian cuisine enthusiasts. The location is excellent, and the restaurant itself boasts a large, well-stocked bar and a calming yet well-lit ambiance. Offering both comfortable indoor and outdoor seating, Yazu sets a sophisticated stage for a memorable meal.

We kicked off our evening with a selection of inventive cocktails. The Orange Cinnamon was an immediate winner; the classic pairing of cinnamon with whiskey never fails to impress. For something different, the Sakura Chan was a strong yet beautifully balanced cocktail, blending sake, gin, lemon, and kaffir for a delightful sweet kick.

The small plates menu offered some absolute treasures. The Yazu Signature Spicy Lamb was a testament to the chef's skill—slow-cooked to tender perfection, the meat was incredibly flavorful and a fantastic choice. The Prawn Tempura Roll was equally fabulous, proving that Yazu excels at classic Japanese favorites.

We also sampled the delightful Pan Fried Chicken Shanghai Dimsums, which were as good as imagined, perfectly complemented by the spicy Shanghai sauce. The Crispy Chicken Cheung Fun, a traditional Cantonese rice noodle roll, was a pleasant surprise, with the crispy chicken adding an excellent textural element.

For the mains, the Chicken Donburi with Veggies was a wonderfully comforting and flavorful bowl. The combination of chicken, teriyaki sauce, and fresh veggies served over Japanese sticky rice was a harmonious blend that we absolutely loved.

To conclude our feast, the Blueberry Cheesecake delivered a stellar performance. It was a fantastic execution of a classic dessert—mesmerizingly good.

Overall, Yazu clearly invests heavily in ensuring a high-quality experience for every patron. From the strong cocktails to the perfectly executed Pan Asian dishes, we had a truly great time and highly recommend Yazu for a sophisticated dining experience.

A special mention to Pravin for making our dinning experience smooth and memorable, name_person=Afreen Ansari}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Brunch, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=2 months ago, review=We visited Yazu Andheri for their Sunday Brunch, and it turned out to be an absolute treat. The variety on offer was impressive — from soul-warming soups and vibrant salads to delicate dimsum and flavour-packed mains, there was something to please every palate. The menu felt thoughtfully curated, offering both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options without compromising on creativity or taste.

Among the standouts were the Truffle Edamame Dumplings and Cream Cheese Dumplings — both silky, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The Sriracha Chicken Dumplings were spicy and juicy, while the Prawn XO Dumplings delivered that perfect seafood punch. From the sushi section, the Spicy Salmon Roll and Crispy Avocado & Cucumber Roll were fresh and delicious — a must-try for sushi lovers.

Tried the brunch buffet with a gang of 8 people. Ambience and atmosphere of the place was superb but the food and service was not upto the hype. Starters are served at the table while main course, soups and desserts are buffet styled. Refills of starters took time. Water is not served unless we ask. Sushi and live pasta was awesome. Pasta chef was quick and awesome. All rice dishes and curries tasted stale. Salad bar was average. Deserts were all usual and nothing drool worthy. They have an ala carte menu too. The buffet spread had a great variety of dishes — both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options — with good balance between Indian and continental flavors. The starters and desserts were definitely the highlights!

The vibe and ambiance were truly elite and happening, with a fantastic live music performance running in the background, which added a vibrant and energetic touch to the whole atmosphere. It was the perfect place to unwind and enjoy a great evening.

The buffet was impressive, offering a wide variety of delicacies in both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options, all served at a very reasonable budget. The flavors were rich and well-balanced, making every dish worth trying. The only minor drawback was that the appetizers arrived with a bit of delay, but honestly, they were so delicious that the wait was completely worth it.

Among the vegetarian options, the Zafrani Paneer was exceptionally flavorful, with a perfect blend of spices. The Shanghai Momos were soft, well-prepared, and bursting with taste, while the Noodle Soup was soothing and had just the right kick. However, the true star was the Lotus Stem dish – a must-try for any food lover. It had a great texture and a uniquely delightful taste that stood out in the whole buffet.

Overall, Mitron offers a fantastic combination of great food, lively ambiance, and good value for money. Whether you are visiting for a casual dinner or a special occasion, this place definitely deserves a spot on your must-visit list. As we arrived at the gate amidst a drizzle, the staff helped us with umbrellas to keep us dry—such a thoughtful gesture that set the tone for the experience ahead.

As we entered the restaurant, the first thing we noticed was its striking red theme—this vibrant color was prominently used throughout the ambience.

We settled into a comfortable spot offered by the staff and ordered a variety of dishes featuring chicken, cheese, and salad, accompanied by whiskey.

Overall experience was good, I wanted to give 4 star from my side.

* Environment and Cleanliness
* For food taste

I visited the place today. Mocktails & appetizers were amazing. The vegetable dumplings were unique. Mr Yogesh, the manager, offered me personalised services; the other servers were equally helpful and absolutely friendly. The main Course was average - I tasted some French Beans and Chicken. In the deserts, the Wasabi Cheese Case was fantastic.

Visit 3 [ Extract ]

Some of the dishes I had:

Duck [ in the main course, whose precise name I don't remember ] - Unusually strong on species, very much unauthentic, some pieces covered almost entirely in bones, and tough to chew upon. Call it a botched preparation and mood spoiler! It's not very often that I leave behind any dish. The grievance was resolved amicably.

Pork baos - You don't get these in many same-level restaurants, so a must-try. On a sweeter side and minced well and soft to consume. Arrived in the estimated time.

The quantity for all the dishes was above average and probably the largest I have seen at same-level restaurants.

Visit 4

A supreme and unforgettable experience

Some of the dishes I tried:

Traditional Pecking Duck - A conventional Chinese dish which is usually served with pancakes, troika of sauces, some veggies, and ofcourse, the duck cuts. Kudos to the chef, on my request, for serving me ready-made and saving me all the effort. The dish was slightly on the sweeter side, and the rolls had a good proportion of duck. Much laborious to scoff if all constituents are served separately.

Steamed Chilean Sea Bass - Prepared in soya ginger sauce, lightly spicy, mildly  pungent, and medium in size. Delicious, healthy and a must try. Maybe a few veggies at the side should be considered.

Light Breeze mocktail - Indeed light, mild soda, simple as it gets. Kinda like virgin mojito less Sprite/7UP and less coriander.

Grapefruit-based mocktail - the best of the three, authentic grapefruit flavour with medium bitterness, preserving the original taste, no soda.

Watermelon-based mocktail - another light one with no soda, pure watermelon [ and no syrup ] and a dash of cucumber.

I would like to thank Mr Jojo for preparing tailor-made off-the-menu [ above-mentioned ] mocktails, all of which were served inside 10 mins. And not to forget, offering me cashews which were off-the-menu. At the end, he also made an exception and served me the desserts from another restaurant because I didn't want any from the menu courtesy to various reasons.

This is amongst the handful of restaurants in this range where almost all the dishes are available in small and large sizes, and this allows one to make better selections on quantity. To add to that, even small sizes are equivalent to medium in many dishes. If I were to offer a suggestion, it would be to rejig the currently-mediocre dessert menu and add dishes like creme brulee, coconut pudding and cheese cake. On the embellishments front, I would say the restaurant is slightly behind despite the fact that they have a Chinese dragon hanging from the top & and a plush red carpet albeit the latter doesn't cover the flooring of the whole restaurant . The pots don't look very attractive and there is room for vibrance - a few paintings & art pieces could help. The restaurant size is quite big with 10+ tables.

It was also nice to meet & have an interlocution with Mr Srinivas, and I would like to thank him for personally overseeing the dinner and ensuring that it was a memorable experience. It is recherche of someone of his level to come down and discuss the ways certain past flaws were handled and briefing on the feedback taken to minimise the bitter moments; I really appreciate this commitment.

The warm welcome with a mogra gajra was such a beautiful, thoughtful touch \u2014 it immediately put a smile on my face.\\n\\nI started off with some mocktails \u2014 Tropical Sunrise (orange juice, rose syrup, lime & soda), Berry Blast (strawberry & lime), and Blue Alaska (minty, Cura\u00e7ao-based mocktail). Each one was refreshing, perfectly balanced, and beautifully presented.\\n\\nComing to the starters \u2014 I went all out!\\n\u2022\\tBhatti ka Murgh \u2013 tender, smoky, and cooked to perfection.\\n\u2022\\tGhost ka Ghilawat \u2013 melt-in-the-mouth mutton galouti kebab served with ulte tawe ka paratha; this one was an absolute star.\\n\u2022\\tLazeez-e-Ghost Seekh \u2013 juicy, well-spiced, and bursting with flavor.\\n\u2022\\tKarare Dahi ke Kebab \u2013 crispy on the outside, soft and creamy inside, absolutely delicious.\\n\\nFor the mains, I had Laal Mirch ka Kukkad paired with Cheese Garlic Naan and Roomali Roti \u2014 the perfect comfort combo. The curry was bold, rich, and full of that authentic Mughlai warmth that just hits the right spot.\\n\\nTo end the evening, I indulged in Angoori Rasmalai, which was soft, chilled, and the perfect level of sweetness to wrap up such a flavorful meal.\\n\\nThe service was exceptional \u2014 polite, attentive, and well-timed. The staff made sure everything was served just right without being intrusive.\\n\\nOverall, Namak is the perfect destination if you\u2019re craving authentic Indian and Mughlai food in a truly luxurious setting. The flavors, presentation, and hospitality are all top-notch. Highly recommend visiting for a cozy dinner or a special occasion.\\n\\n\u2728 My Rating: 5/5\\n\\uD83C\\uDF38 Ambience: 5/5\\n\\uD83C\\uDF74 Food: 5/5\\n\\uD83D\\uDC68\u200d\\uD83C\\uDF73 Service: 5/5\\n\\uD83D\\uDCAB Overall Experience: 5/5\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b92,000+\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE\":[\"2_people\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Julia Asmus\",\"time_line\":\"2 months ago\",\"review\":\"The good: The food was delicious (if a bit overpriced, but that comes with eating at a hotel restaurant)\\n\\nThe not so good: Food and drinks took ages to arrive. **Appetizers:** The *Lavash Kebab* and *Kebab Halabi* were absolutely delicious — soft, juicy, and full of flavour.

**Drinks:** Tried *Smoky Rum N Raisins* and *Palm Islands*, both were refreshing and beautifully presented.

**Main Course:** *Shawarma Al Bayroute* and *Arayes Tavuk* were perfectly cooked — rich taste, great portion size, and authentic flavour.

The overall theme is Turkish with very welcoming interiors. Loved the hot air balloon themed decor. The outside area is also nice for gatherings.

Although above average on cost, each of their offerings do stand out in terms of presentation and the experience. No wonder it takes around 20 mins prep time, the wait is much worth it.

The Al Meshwi non-veg platter was more than enough for the three of us with assortment of starters. The different dips and pickled vegetables provided were also very fresh.

The star of the day was Machboos Al Kuzu, which is a very rich lamb and rice dish similar to the Yemeni Mandi. I wish they had not discontinued the regular Mandi, which was lighter on stomach for picky eaters.

To end it we had their signature Baklava, the presentation of which stunned us with quite a showmanship with flash frozen rose flower. It tasted amazing paired with gulkhand icecream.

Happy with the service with very knowledgeable people who patiently explained to us what each dish was. Great for family outings. Would love to go again !, name_person=Jyothis Thaliath}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 months ago, review=Just had the most incredible dining experience at this stunning Middle Eastern restaurant in Powai, Mumbai! 🤩 The moment I stepped in, I was transported to the vibrant streets of the Middle East, surrounded by mesmerizing decor and plush ambiance 🌿✨.

I started with not one, but TWO signature drinks - "Let's Date" and "Honey on Fire" 🍹🔥. Both were absolute perfection, with the sweetness of dates and honey balanced by the subtle kick of spices. Definitely a must-try for any cocktail enthusiast! 🍸

For the main course, I indulged in some finger-licking goodies:
- *Kataifi Prawns*: Crispy, succulent prawns wrapped in kataifi pastry, bursting with flavors of the Middle East 🍤
- *Kebab Joojeh*: Tender, juicy chicken kebabs marinated in a blend of spices and yogurt, grilled to perfection 🍗
- *Harissa Chicken Manakeish*: Spicy harissa chicken on a bed of crispy dough, topped with melted cheese and herbs - a flavor bomb! 🧀
- *Moroccan Lemon Olive Chicken*: Zesty, herby, and utterly delicious, this dish was a masterclass in balancing flavors 🍗

And no meal is complete without dessert! 🍰 I ended my meal with the classic *Turkish Baklava*, layers of flaky phyllo pastry, crunchy nuts, and sweet honey... it was love at first bite! ❤️

The aesthetic ambiance, complete with air balloons, added to the magic of the evening. The courteous staff made sure we felt right at home. 🌟

Perfect spot for a date or a night out with friends! 📅👫 Highly recommend! 👏, name_person=Kshitija Bhosale}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=Visited Bayroute, a premier Middle Eastern restaurant, and had such a lovely experience. The ambiance is beautiful warm lighting, elegant decor, & a very comfortable vibe. The staff was really helpful and attentive throughout our visit.
We tried two mocktails Reyhan and Watermelon Cooler, both refreshing and nicely made.
For food, we had Feta and Pine Nut Stuffed Falafel, Harissa Chicken Kebab, Musabbaha, and Koshari. The falafel was crispy on the outside and soft inside with a rich filling of feta and pine nuts. At that price point, you expect truly exceptional creativity, presentation, or ingredients, but these were simply average. Otherwise, it feels excessive and out of proportion to what you’re actually getting.

We had dined the night before at Bastian at the Top, and the contrast was striking. Bastian was on another level entirely — the views from the 47th floor, the energy, the food, the drinks, and even the value for money were all significantly better. Rating: 3.5/5 stars", name_person=Lakshita Agarwal}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Breakfast, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Classic_Hakka_Steam_Dimsum_Platter, Dark_Chocolate_Mousse_with_Mandarin_Sorbet, Soup, Half_Peking_Duck], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=11 months ago, review=Had the pleasure of dining at Hakkasan in Mumbai, and I have to say, the atmosphere is fantastic. The setting is modern and sleek, with comfortable seating and a stylish bar that creates a welcoming vibe. It’s definitely one of the top Chinese restaurants in Mumbai, but while the ambiance is spot on, it doesn’t quite deliver in terms of traditional Chinese authenticity.

The staff were friendly and attentive, always ready to assist. We ordered the Peking duck, which was, unfortunately, underwhelming. The preparation was just okay—the skin wasn’t crispy, and the duck itself was on the smaller side but came from Thailand. Traditionally, the creases would be used for a soup or stir-fry, but they were left unused here. A bit disappointing considering the cost and overall taste.

On a positive note, the dim sum was quite good, and I was impressed by how they cater to a wide range of dietary preferences, with no lard used in their offerings. We also tried the stir-fried buffalo, which was surprisingly delicious—tender, not too gamey, and packed with flavor.

The drinks were excellent, and it would’ve been nice to see the tea served personally as needed, perhaps with a selection of puer on the menu for added depth?

As for dessert, I think they could elevate the experience by adding some authentic Chinese options instead of just only the Western-style desserts.

The desserts, while good, leaned more towards Western-style offerings. I would love to see some traditional Chinese desserts added to the menu for an authentic touch.

All in all, it was a very enjoyable experience. The service was excellent, and the atmosphere was top-notch, though there’s room for improvement in the authenticity and food preparation. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Peri_Peri_Chicken_Pizza, French_Fries], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a year ago, review=I recently had the pleasure of visiting Tales of Tavern, and it was an enjoyable experience from start to finish. The assorted choices ensure there's something for everyone, making it a great spot for group outings.

One of the highlights of the buffet was the inclusion of pizza. It's not often you find such a staple comfort food included in a buffet spread, and it did not disappoint. The pizzas were well-cooked with a perfect blend of toppings, appealing to both adults and kids alike.

The ambiance of Tales of Tavern is another strong point. The decor is thoughtfully designed, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere that is perfect for both casual lunches and lively dinner parties. Although I visited for lunch, I could easily see how this place would transform into a fantastic dinner and party venue. The lighting, music, and overall vibe make it an ideal spot for evening gatherings.

In conclusion, Tales of Tavern is a well-rounded pub that excels in offering a diverse and delicious buffet. The ambiance of the restaurant is inviting and spacious, with comfortable seating arrangements suitable for both small and large groups. The decor is modern yet cozy, creating a pleasant dining atmosphere.
The service provided by the staff is commendable. They are attentive, friendly, and prompt in attending to the needs of the customers.
The buffet started with a refreshing mocktail but was much needed to beat the summer heat.
Coming to the food...
We started with an aromatic chicken clear soup which had it's flavours infused in every bit of a drop.
The starters offered in the lunch buffet are diverse and flavorful. The Paneer Hariyali Kebab is a standout, with tender paneer marinated in aromatic green herbs. The Potato Yellow Chilly and Black Pepper Chilly provide a spicy kick, while the Chicken Alishan Kebab and Chicken Harissa Wings are perfect for meat lovers with their juicy and succulent flavors. 🍗
The main course selection offers a variety of options catering to different tastes. The Herb Rice is fragrant and perfectly cooked, complementing the Spicy Black Bean Sauce which adds a rich and bold flavor. The Veg Kolhapuri bursts with traditional Indian spices, while the Chicken Kadai and Grilled Chicken with Rojan Sauce are both tender and flavorful. The Dal Tadka is a comforting addition, providing a perfect balance of lentils and spices.
It also had a seperate Pizza and Salad Bar 🍕
The inclusion of Veg Pizza and Tandoori Chicken Pizza adds a Western touch to the buffet, with both options being delicious and freshly prepared. The Salad Bar offers a refreshing assortment of options, including Nachos with Salsa, Russian Salad, Chicken Sauces Salad, Beetroot Hummus & Pita, and a vibrant Mix Fruit Platter, providing a healthy and light complement to the meal.
The dessert selection is the perfect conclusion to the meal. The Biscoff Cheesecake is a heavenly delight, with its creamy texture and indulgent flavor. The assorted pastries are beautifully presented and offer a variety of sweet treats to satisfy any sweet tooth. 🍰
In conclusion, the lunch buffet at Tales of Tavern in CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai, is a delightful culinary experience that caters to a variety of tastes. With its diverse selection of starters, main courses, pizza, salads, and desserts, coupled with excellent service and inviting ambiance, this restaurant truly stands out as a top dining destination in the area. Whether you're craving traditional Indian flavors or international delights, there's something for everyone for just Rs 799/-

My dining experience at Dakshin in ITC Grand Central, Mumbai, was nothing short of extraordinary. Renowned for its authentic South Indian fare, the restaurant offers curated vegetarian and non-vegetarian thalis, each highlighting signature dishes from the southern states of India.

Tomato Pappu from Andhra Pradesh, a tangy and comforting lentil dish.
Padupe from Mangalore, Karnataka, a flavorful, lightly spiced preparation.
Uruli Roast from Tamil Nadu, a deliciously spiced vegetarian delicacy.
Jamin Mangachoru from Kerala, a fragrant mango-infused rice preparation.
Venchana Mamsam from Andhra Pradesh, a richly spiced mutton dish.
Accompaniments like Pachadi, a cooling yogurt-based dish, and the aromatic Koli Biryani, completed the non-vegetarian thali.

We stayed for four days in this beautiful hotel and it was a great experience - but not the harbour bar.
We should have be warned right after entering: no friendly hello from the staff and worst 90s pop songs played way too lout from a DJ (btw: who needs a DJ for that most mainstream unpersonal song selection?).

The interior design is kind of post modern Art Deco but far from being cozy or cool.
*But now for the drinks.*:
One of the reviewers praised them for the story that would be behind each of the signature drinks.
Well, the bar menu mentions a story for each signature drink. But there is no recognisable connection between the story and the drink.
And there is not even necessarily a connection between drink description and drink. Or would you expect a garden salad with plenty of cucumber seeds that fills one third of your glass when only white rum, vodka, lime and syrup are mentioned in the menu? And
One could overlook this, if the two signature drinks we had, would have convinced by creativity and taste. But they didn’t, not at all.
The best signature drinks become classics some day. A good signature drink makes you remember drink and location. These unbalanced drinks we won’t remember.
And: how does the great Gregory Peck deserve to have such a mediocre drink named after him?

[{'name_person': 'sam mahtani', 'time_line': 'a month ago', 'review': 'Mumbai, and especially Bandra West (with another outlet in Churchgate), should be delighted to welcome Mezcalita—a bright and comfortable Mexican cantina/taquería. The service, led by Pinku and his team, is caring, attentive, and genuinely warm, while the food strikes a perfect balance between creativity and authenticity.

The menu is vibrant and visually engaging, guiding guests toward a true Mexican culinary adventure, with comfort food taking center stage.

The Guacamole (GUAC), made with fresh Hass avocados, delivers a creamy texture and rich, buttery flavor. Blended with tomatoes, onions, a dash of lime, and a subtle kick of habanero chilies, it is simply delicious and divine.

I  was especially blown away by the habanero-laced cottage cheese cubes, paired with soy protein and other fresh ingredients. This appetizer is packed with flavor and offers great value for money. Pro tip: always pair it with a glass of Horchata—Mexico’s national drink—made from rice milk, cardamom, cinnamon, and both evaporated and condensed milk.

Mezcalita also shows its sensibility by baking its own bread for the Tortas (Mexican sandwiches). The Telera buns, with their crisp crust and fluffy interior, elevate the experience. The cottage cheese Chilaquiles Torta was an absolute delight.

The black bean vegetarian burritos were impressively well-balanced and just the right size for a single taster portion.

For your next Mexican culinary journey, head to Mezcalita at Pali Hill. Explore their wide range of cocktails, and don’t hesitate to reach out to Pinku, the manager, for a thoughtfully chosen table.

Final note: Mezcalita isn’t just a restaurant—it’s a celebration of Mexican flavors brought to life with care, creativity, and authenticity. The staff has not been trained, the quantities are horribly limited, the ingredients are sub par and the chef & waiters are unable to answer any questions or incorporate any feedback - the PVR team has not trained them adequately and seem to be content with ripping off their customers.

If you’re an Asian food lover, this place should definitely be on your list!

I’ve ordered from Chimichurri several times, but this was my first visit to their Time Square branch. The restaurant is quite spacious, but if you’re looking for a quiet spot, this might not be it; the loud music keeps the vibe buzzing, and the crowd gets equally lively. The staff, however, are warm and friendly, which balances things out nicely.

The restaurant is located on the ground floor, right before Persian Darbar. The décor is clean and neat, and the seating is super comfortable; perfect for long conversations and chill hangouts with friends

P.S. The dimsums here are a must-try, especially the assorted platter. They’re awesome!

Would I recommend it? Absolutely, yes.

I ordered the Spring Hill Cooler cocktail, snapper as my main, and finished with a Blondie Sunrise coffee. The snapper was definitely the highlight — the green chutney-style marinade worked really well with the fish and the texture was smooth and flavorful. I was initially considering the crab rice, but in hindsight the snapper felt like the right choice since it was lighter.

The cocktail was good but slightly on the sweeter side for my taste; next time I might try the Bano Picante, which sounds like it would bring a bit more spice. The coffee at the end was okay, nothing particularly special.

The views from the restaurant are impressive, although visibility was a bit low during the day. I imagine the experience would be even better in the evening. The interiors are stylish, with high ceilings that make the space feel open and interesting.

Despite being located at a busy intersection, the instant you come inside, you are taken to a tranquil and unexpectedly quiet environment. FOOD:
Vegetable Cheese Rissois: Though the classic Portuguese fried pastry is usually filled with meat, we tried the vegetarian version and were not disappointed. It starts with a crumbly-soft bite which leads to a minced vegetables mixed with cheese that definitely melts in your mouth.

Mapusa Market toast with Cheese & Green Chilli: Coconut boys take on the chilli cheese toast with a twist. On first look it’s just your average cheese chilli toast, but one bite into it and you hit a tangy punch which took us by surprise…. Choris Chilli Fry: Choriz tossed with chilli, onion, tomato teamed up with warm, fluffy poee… we absolutely left licking our fingers. Would have gone for round two but there was more to be relished on the menu.

Mushroom & vegetables slow cooked with Xacuti masala: A medley of steamed veggies (Mushroom, carrot, potato, cauliflower) tossed in a Xacuti gravy. You have an option of Poee or steamed rice to accompany it and we went with the latter. Serradura: This simple pudding can go awry in so many ways… And believe me, we've tasted some absolute disasters. But coconut boy absolutely nailed-it! The crumbly, biscuit dust alternated with fluffy, light whipped cream was what we devoured at the end of a great meal. Not too sweet, not too dense… just perfect.

Service: The service undoubtedly elevated our entire experience! We had Siddhesh giving us amazing recommendations and making sure we had everything we needed. reviews:
["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=The Bombay Earth is one of the restaurants out of the many others in the premises of Eskay resorts ,it's a pure vegetarian restaurant which offers you some amazing mocktails and some decent cocktails.
The presentation of mocktails is really something to look out for and some decent work done in the cocktail as well.
The restaurant is quite spacious and usually people come over here in groups for kitty parties and normal dine in .
They offer membership to the resort and also discounts are offered to their members as well on their food bills.

The Vibes of this place is really positive and soothing , the staff is welcoming and sweet to talk.
They gave us some really good suggestions for trying some amazing stuff especially the spinach smoothies which was a shocker to me as I hate spinach , but it turned out to be a blunder .

What we tried goes out like this -

▶️Mocktails
1) Cranberry kiss - from presentation to the taste , from edible flowers at the top to the cranberry and grenadine taste along with the orange juice Everything was perfectly balanced in this amazing Mocktail , highly recommended 🔴

2)Spinach Smoothie - I literally was surprised to hear that it's a spinach smoothie but by the looks it looks decent and the amazin artwork of lemon at the top for presentation was really worth the wait , the mixture of spinach and some kiwi literally didn't make it feel as if I was having spinach smoothie , something which was really worth a try ..

▶️Cocktails
1) Choco Martini -good old cocktail made with coffee liqueur mixed with coffee powder topped with whiskey...every sip was refreshing when coffee liqueur hits your palate

2) Activated Batman - something unique and must try drink ...edible charcoal shaked with whiskey garnish with pineapple sticks...taste was unique as were the ingredients in it

▶️Appetizers
1)Kung pao Potatoes - Chinese style potato fries tossed in Kung pao sauce garnished with sesame seeds... perfectly balanced sweet and sourtaste hits the right note.

2) Tandoori platter - a platter consisting of all the options in the menu from cauliflower to baby potatoes to mushrooms to baby corn Everything was available in the Platter , Different exotic vegetables marinated with different sauces and made up on tandoor , achari aloo was my favourite marinated dish, and so was the baby corn , not to forget the paneer was also delicious the achari seekh kebabs can be a lil juicy as they became a lil dry  , but a good blend very soft and yummy , overall a good platter .

▶️Main course
1)Pot rice -  a mixture of many veggies and loads of rice though the presentation is something that can be worked on the tomatoes at the side make it look more Indian otherwise the taste of the dish is really good to have , the veggies are diced nicely and make it really healthy and a flavour full potrice , enough for two people quite fullfilling and  worth the penny.

▶️Desserts
Mango cream - Seasonal dessert consist of whipped cream mixed with mango juice and garnished with slice of mango slice ,it's the summer special dish and since it's mango season they have mango cream in their dessert section which is presented quite  beautifully and the glass filled with cream and mango juice giving it the sweet and sour taste , making it really delicious and something you should definitely try in the mango special season.highly recommended 🔴

Overall the service is good  , the management is really sweet though they take a lil time which they can improve other then that it's a really good place to look out for , an amazing place for a veggie lover and for someone who wishes to relax and get out of the noise of the city it's a perfect hideout place ., name_person=Sagar Kantharia Foodie_mumbaikar7}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=5 years ago, review=Recently visited this amazing outlet at eskay resorts called the Bombay earth. The food was really excellent. The quantity was lovely. It was worth visiting it. Would love to visit this place again for sure.

Torii in Bandra came highly recommended\u2014and spoiler alert\u2014it almost lives up to the hype, and then some.\\n\\nLet\u2019s start from the outside: that black-and-white arched entrance with the gold-lettered TORII feels like you\u2019re about to enter a movie set. Inside, the vibe is unmistakably plush\u2014with mirrored ceilings, retro lampshades, opulent seating, and music that doesn\u2019t scream at you but keeps the energy flowing. It\u2019s where Japanese zen meets Mumbai glam.\\n\\nThe Meal\\nWe were 7. The table bill read \u20b945,999, so yes, about \u20b96.5K per head after taxes and service, but here\u2019s what made it feel worth it:\\n\u2022\\tCold Young Coconut Carpaccio \u2013 Sounds fancy and tasted the part. Light, tropical, and a perfect start.\\n\u2022\\tMiso Black Cod \u2013 Showstopper dish. Silky, melt-in-mouth. It\u2019s what black cod dreams are made of.\\n\u2022\\tChicken Chilli Oil & Lemongrass Chicken Tsukune \u2013 Packed flavour bombs. The chilli oil was a standout.\\n\u2022\\tCold Prawns Tempura Maki \u2013 Crisp, clean, and a hit with everyone at the table.\\n\u2022\\tTwilight Tingles (mocktail) \u2013 Refreshing and not sugary, a tough balance to nail.\\n\u2022\\tTorii X-mess Sundae \u2013 The name may be cheeky, but this dessert brought childlike joy with its waffle castle presentation. The kind of ending you photograph before devouring.\\n\\nService\\nSmooth, attentive, and non-intrusive. Our server knew the menu well and paced the meal right. The lounge is located inside Palm Beach Galleria Mall, Sector 19D, Vashi, Navi Mumbai – on the rooftop, just like other popular spots in the building.

The total bill came to ₹6688 (including taxes). Here’s what we ordered:

2 Butter Rotis – ₹109 each
1 Butter Chicken – ₹669
5 Butter Naans – ₹99 each
1 Cheesy Fries – ₹384
3 Fresh Lime Sodas – ₹210 each
1 Hakka Noodles – ₹428
1 Murg Tikka Masala – ₹637
1 Non-Veg Platter – ₹1499
3 Virgin Mojitos – ₹440 each
1 Water Bottle – ₹90

The ambience was nice, and although they had live music, it hadn’t started by the time we were there, so we missed out on that part of the experience. Still, the setting was good for a small group celebration.

The food quality was very nice, and everyone at the table enjoyed what was served. Service was decent, and the overall vibe of the place felt modern and chill.

However, the one major disappointment was the pricing of the water bottle — ₹90 for a Bisleri bottle with MRP of ₹20 felt extremely unnecessary and overpriced. For larger groups, these small add-ons can become an unpleasant surprise on the final bill. That part definitely felt like a setback.

To begin with, the vegetarian selection was extremely limited, which itself was disappointing for a premium luxury hotel. What made it worse was that several items had already run out by around 9:30–10 PM, which is surprisingly early for a dinner buffet. The veg sushi, in particular, was tucked away inside the refrigerator with no proper labelling or indication—it genuinely felt like a game of hide-and-seek unless you already knew where to look.

We were excited to try the chaat and gol gappas (puchkas), but this was hands down the worst part of the experience. Service suffered due to severe understaffing. The staff, though polite, seemed unsure of menu details themselves, and the small dining arena with closly sat tables, which further affected the overall experience.

Overall, this dinner experience was a 5/10 at best. As Accor Gold members who genuinely love Accor properties, this was by far one of the most disappointing dining experiences we’ve had in recent times. Sadly, we wouldn’t recommend Pondicherry Café for vegetarian diners and do not see ourselves returning anytime soon.

I recently visited Pondicherry Café at Sofitel in Mumbai, and unfortunately, the experience fell far below expectations. Here’s a detailed breakdown of my visit:

Parking Hassle

As someone who arrived on a motorbike, the experience began with a significant disappointment. The hotel does not provide motorbike parking within its premises. Instead, I was directed to a pay-and-park lot 300 meters away, located on an open ground opposite Jio International School. This parking area was poorly maintained and inconvenient, especially for those with huge bikes like mine. I had to leave my bike without a handle locked, which was unsettling.

Walking from the parking lot to the hotel in the scorching sun further diminished the experience. For a luxury hotel, this lack of accommodation for bikers is surprising and disheartening.

Ambience and Atmosphere

Once inside, the ambience of Pondicherry Café was pleasant but lacked any accompanying music, which made it feel somewhat lifeless. The décor was appealing, but the overall atmosphere could use some warmth and vibrance to match the expectations of a premium dining experience.

Buffet Experience

We opted for the buffet based on its promising menu, but the food did not deliver in terms of taste. While there was a variety of options available, very few stood out. Here’s a breakdown of the meal:
•	Soup: 2/5 – Bland and unremarkable.
•	Starters: 3/5 – Only two items were decent; the rest were forgettable.
•	Main Course: 2/5 – A disappointing selection with subpar flavors.
•	Desserts: 2/5 – Average at best. The pista kulfi had an odd paan flavor, which didn’t appeal to me.
•	Pizza & Pasta: Possibly the worst I’ve ever had.

Overall, the food lacked flavor and quality, especially considering the premium pricing.

Service

The service was another letdown. Staff were hard to find when needed, whether it was for cutlery or water. This lack of attentiveness added to the frustration and further detracted from the overall dining experience.

Final Thoughts

For a restaurant within a luxury hotel, Pondicherry Café failed to meet expectations on multiple fronts. The motorbike parking issue, coupled with an underwhelming dining experience, made this visit quite disappointing. Considering the high ratings this restaurant holds on platforms like Zomato and Google, I feel it is overrated.

Recommendation:
•	For Bikers: Avoid this place if you value convenience and proper parking facilities.
•	For Food Lovers: There are far better dining options in the BKC area offering superior taste, service, and overall experience at similar or lower price points.

Overall Rating:
•	Ambience: 3/5
•	Food Taste: 2/5
•	Service: 2/5
•	Value for Money: 1/5

["{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Visited here some time back  for dinner and had a pretty good experience. The food was decent but the ambience could be better. The live tabla music does not go with vibe of the restaurant. The veg options are pretty limited and we called for pretty much all of them. The Mac and cheese poppers and the pizza inspired arrancini were great and you must definitely order that. The charcoal sandwich and falafel squares can be skipped. We called for 2 sushi out of which the tempura one barely had any tempura however the spiced avocado was nice. The crystal dumplings as well as the edamame dumplings were good but the edamame one was very spicy. In mains, we got the baked gnocchi which was too cheesy and barely had any potato. The highlight of the meal was the simply chocolate dessert! The brownie and profiterole were absolutely delicious. Would go again only for that. All in all, for veg Options are limited and not worth paying so much for., name_person=Sachi Gandhhi}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Illuminati

“Beautiful things and Delicious food is priceless.” It’s a thought come to my mind when I’ve visited newly opened place in BKC named Illuminati. This place surprises me in my first visit. As you entered the place, it’s a different world altogether.

This place certainly raises the bar chicness and opulence. With all positive vibes and great hospitality Illuminati won accolades.

The place lit with beautiful white lights, classy décor and huge bar. They have a wide collection of Alcohol and wines.

The amazing indulgence of spices and the flavors has made me their fan. The varied menu has really tempted my taste buds and taken it to a niche.

So, first let’s start with cocktails and then food.

Prisoner: Vodka based (kettle one) with Galangal and Lemongrass. Loved the freshness and sweet taste because of lemongrass.

Blue Fairy: Jim Beam + Blueberry + Blue Pea Bitters + Orange slice. Looks amazing but tasted less of alcohol. Maybe not stirred well, still can give a try.

Believer: Believe me, it’s the best one among all three. Kettle One Vodka+ Chamomile spiced Apple + Thyme. Really amazing. This was smooth, fresh and bit different.

Quick Steamed Rawas Xiao Xing: Loved the balance. Bold flavors. Very smooth texture. Presentation is beautiful. Rawas fish is served with Xiao Xing wine. Overall colourful and made well. Do try.

Tokyo Chicken Karrage: This looks amazing and tasted so good, crunchy. You can taste both sweet and spicy at the same time. I could actually feel the distinct flavors yet intact.

Tempura Prawn: It delectably delights you. One of the best tempura prawn sushi I had in recent time. Tasted lovely.

Chicken and Bok Choy: It was simply great. Bok Choi is a type of Chinse Cabbage. Minced Chicken and Bok Choy has a generous stuffing. Served hot. Do try.

Honey Sesame Chicken Bowl: I still cannot get over this. The star dish of the day. Diced chicken tossed in sticky sesame soy with a bit of 5 pickled chillies. All the herbs intact and served with Jasmine rice was a delicious treat to my gluttony.

The Decadent Cake French Toast: Not too sweet. But not to be miss for sure.

Time and again I would just sing praises for this absolutely amazing place which makes sure to lure its patron and woo them with delicious offerings.

P.S: The review is strictly depending on my personal experience.

They’ve got fab, black and white interiors and seating complementing the whole aura of the place. They’ve got a whole ambiance that commands respect and denotes class through and through.

The food carries multiple cuisines - indian, Chinese, Thai and continental and they showcase some signature dishes with a twist. Plating is exceptionally beautiful with singular portion sizes meals. Here’s what we ate:

1. Fish and chips poppers - all fried elements with a mushy peas, potato cheese poppers and fried Rawas. Served with some spicy remoulade.

2. Pomegranate Molasses lamb chops - these were beautifully shaped lamb medallions that were soaked in a sweet sauce. The predominant flavours were sweet, tangy and creamy and was delicious.

3. Chicken and prawns suimai dimsums - these were cute little balls of flavour with a taut coating.

4. Jasmine steamed Rawas with lemongrass prawns broth - the Rawas was steamed to fall apart on touch perfection and had undertones of jasmine to it. The broth had a strong flavour of tomato. Served on a bed of noodles with prawn crackers it was quite an art in its presentation.

5. Chilli crusted prawns with tabbouleh - the crust was soft and the prawns were fresh. Loved the tabbouleh served along with it.

6. Confit duck leg with medjool date purée - the duck leg was tender, juicy and the added skin was just a brilliant addition to it. The date purée added a new dimension and lifted the dish. Enjoyed it.

8. Jasmine chicken fried rice - the chicken fried rice was really pearly and quite delicious. Loved it.

9. Decadent cake french Toast - The bade was a pound cake instead of bread which was fried with an egg dip. Was served with some vanilla ice cream and some dusting sugar and was simple, yet really heart warming and delicious.

For the drinks we tried some of their mocktails Which were just as good as the food. The Heaven on Earth is a favourite. It’s got the freshness of watermelon accentuated by the light hint of passion fruit and lemongrass. Bloody brilliant.

We were served by Maaz. Service was prompt and courteous. Had a great time and particularly enjoyed the beautiful plating, classy ambiance and their playlist., name_person=The Food Auror}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Illuminati is a newly opened casual dining bar winch serves Asian, Japanese, American and European cuisines with some explicit cocktails and mocktails.

They have really done splendid work with the interiors, as there is major use of glass and elaborate glass work adorning the ceilings and walls.

We had

This was one of the best cocktails I have had. The drink was just perfect. I even loved the way it was presented, with 2 litchies on a stick on the cusp of the glass.

📍Believer

📍 Blue fairy
I have never been the one to try bourbon based cocktails, but I am lucky I tried this one out.

Simply chocolate

If one wants to went out the week's tension and stress and loosen up, then this is the best place as there a live DJ too!, name_person=Saanvi Kanodia}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=From luxury hotels, businesses, to commercial spaces, Bandra-Kurla complex in Mumbai houses some of the biggest names in the industry within its high-rise buildings (most of which look like art-work made in steel and glass!). But for quite a few years now, BKC has also been one of the go-to food destinations of the city. Inspire BKC is one such hotspot which is a commercial hub filled with offices and restaurants. Despite being surrounded by places like Trèsind, Uno Más, Cardboard, Drifters etc., Illuminati manages to stand out and offer something unique of its own.

Illuminati is a unique mix between a lounge, a fine-dine experience and a soon-to-be nightclub. If you have heard about this place or have come across any photos of the place, you have most probably seen how beautiful this place looks. The ambience of this place is phenomenal and the 'starry-night-like' lights make this place seem 'out of this world', quite literally. The combination of unique lighting, the black and white decor and the extensive use of glass make this place feel aesthetically grand. But the premiumness of this place doesn't end here, it also spills down to the culinary options that this place has to offer.
The menu has been curated to cover a variety of cuisines, which include European, Japanese, Italian and American. The food here looked as gorgeous as the place itself, and the taste was amazing too. It is really difficult to take a bad photo in this place, be it the food or the ambience.

Our favourites were Charcoal bread sandwiches and Rajma feta squares, but you couldn't go wrong with anything on the menu. We also quite liked the Pizza inspired arancini and the Spiced edamame hummus. For the mains, we would definitely recommend Baked gnocchi fontina and Braised broccoli & Tofu curry with rice, as some solid vegetarian options.
