We enjoyed almost everything we ordered.\\n\\nWould definitely like to give a shout out to their staff Mridula who was very caring and polite. She took extra effort to make sure we enjoyed the food.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,200\u20131,400\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":4,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":3}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Pratik Gadgil\",\"time_line\":\"a year ago\",\"review\":\"Situated over a fourth of a mile away from the highway, the pan-Asian restaurant Noyna -- inside the relatively new and distinct Taj The Trees -- throws up a plain yet premium background and some sui generis delicacies. The plush blue sofas promise to provide a cosy seating and the complimentary opener -- the sweet and tangy Papaya strips -- is a tempting way to start the proceedings. The masala peanuts -- which come along with those papaya strips -- might find themselves on the eight ball; replacing them with flavoured cashews might just buttress the unfolding and make it impeccable. Ah, that might be a high expectation!\\n\\nI ordered a watermelon mojito and an orange mojito in mocktails; both were fantastic, came within 10 minutes and had more than average sizes when compared to same-star restaurants. As per instructions, both had medium-power soda and were slightly sweet and sour, respectively. In the appetizers, we ordered a Pork Bao, which is available in two sizes -- small and large ( having two and four pieces, respectively ). One can get the same item in other Taj properties in the city, and it is a must-try; the bao was soft and filled with minced pork made in a slightly sweet sauce. In the mains, we ordered Chilean Sea Bass and Chicken Fried Rice. The former was made in an unconventional preparation but it was scrummy; the black pepper sauce made the dish just a tad pungent. The price was comparatively lower than same-star restaurants and the size was average.\\n\\nWhat stood out in particular were the desserts -- the date cake and another one ( whose name I have forgotten ). The former was rich in dates, which came girded by a slightly thick date pudding and topped with vanilla ice cream; it was sweet overall. The latter was amazingly and mildly sour ( and salty ), topped up with an orange syrup, girded by cream shots; vanilla ice cream -- which came by default with this dish -- doesn't pair up well and should be taken out for this dish. Both the desserts tasted authentic, were true to their apposite descriptions and arrived within 10 mins from ordering. We were inside the restaurant well beyond the closing hours and kudos to the staff for ensuring that the experience wasn't compromised.\\n\\nThe hot air balloon emitting dim yellow light is plain looking yet presents a nice aura to sit under for a premium late-night dinner; the richly coloured brown walls deserve a painting or two on them, as is generally the case in such restaurants. One thing the restaurant might want to get fixed quickly is its nameplate, which isn't anywhere where it ideally should be, not even on the face or wall at the entrance of the restaurant ( unlike its North Indian counterpart on the same floor ); this is the first time I have visited any such restaurant whose nameplate is pretty concealed. This certainly couldn't have been a brain fade! This is like a chap introducing himself in detail but forgetting to quote his name. When pointed out the same ( out of curiosity ), the staff showed a bar counter outside the restaurant ( which is a part of the restaurant ) where the name was written, but it wasn't in normal sight, and on top of that, the nameplate was quite overshadowed by the hanging leaves of a branch.\\n\\nThe restaurant menu is neither available on the Taj website nor anywhere else, and this, nearly a year after the inauguration of the restaurant is something, is something that doesn't sound all right.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MODE\":\"Dine in\",\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Merrin Nellary\",\"time_line\":\"9 months ago\",\"review\":\"Had an amazing experience at Nonya..!The food was absolutely delicious, and the service was exceptional. Their attention to detail and hospitality made the celebration even more memorable. Highly recommend this place for a fantastic dining experience!\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Quiet, easy to talk\",\"GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE\":[\"Suitable_for_all_group_sizes\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME\":\"No wait\"}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Parag Pandey\",\"time_line\":\"a year ago\",\"review\":\"Amazing Asian food from the award winning masterchef, Deni Koswara; fantastic service by Piyush and Mrudula; and the warm and wonderful overall experience under the watchful eyes of Anu. All these made for a super experience for us at the 'Nonya' restaurant, at 'Taj Trees', Godrej complex, Vikhroli, Mumbai.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5}}", "{\"name_person\":\"N Angelina\",\"time_line\":\"8 months ago\",\"review\":\"My second time back at Taj the Trees and I make sure I come back to Nonya. I had lunch with Szechuan fried rice with prawns and stir fried green beans. Both dishes were supperb, definitely in my Top 3 for each category. The fried rice was even better with extra Szechuan chili added which they gave as condiments. The burnt garlic flavour, slightly hot chili, and Chinese style fried rice combination is just perfect. Hats off to the friendly Indonesian chef, Pak Koswara.\\nThe service was not proactive enough 6 months ago, today it was spot on. Location & ambience
•	Gallops is located inside the Mahalaxmi Race Course in Mumbai, which gives it a uniquely lush, open-green backdrop uncommon in the city’s dining scene.  ￼
•	The décor and setting combine colonial charm with upscale comfort: for example, walnut-floors, candle-light chandeliers, and equestrian-themed décor post-revamp.  ￼
•	Outdoor and al-fresco dining is one of its strong suits — especially nice in cooler months.  ￼

2. Food quality & menu variety
•	The menu successfully blends Indian and Continental dishes. From traditional kebabs and curries to refined European-style mains, there’s something for varied tastes.  ￼
•	Signature dishes that get strong mentions:
•	“Dori Kebab” (mutton or chicken) – minced, skewered and charcoal-cooked.  ￼
•	“Chicken Ala Kiev” with cheese/butter-filled centre, as a refined European choice.  ￼
•	Desserts are also strong: Baked Alaska and newer additions like Baileys Caramel Cloud.  ￼
•	Many reviewers emphasize the generous portions, good presentation and a sense of value for a fine-dining venue.  ￼

3. Service & experience
•	The service is frequently praised: attentive staff, good recommendations (e.g., for wine or pairings), smooth reservation experience when booked in advance.  ￼
•	The overall dining experience is described as memorable— especially when everything aligns (good table, nice view, well-timed service). For example:
“What a wonderful restaurant from the minute we arrived the staff were so efficient and helpful, the food was absolutely incredible.”  ￼

4. Ideal for special occasions / date nights
•	The ambience, décor and location make it ideal for anniversaries, special dinners or when you want to treat yourself. Many mentions of formative visits, nostalgic moments, photo-friendly setting.  ￼

If I were picking one restaurant for a refined Mumbai meal — especially if you’re after something more than just dinner but an experience — Gallops checks a lot of boxes:
•	A setting that feels premium yet relaxed.
•	A menu that offers both familiar Indian comfort and elevated Continental touches.
•	Good enough service to let you focus on the evening rather than logistics.
•	A chance to dine in one of Mumbai’s less-hustle zones (given the race-course setting) while still being accessible.

If you ask me: go for the outdoor or window-view table (book ahead), order one of the signature starters + a main you haven’t tried, and finish with one of the classic desserts. Nestled right along the coast, the restaurant boasts a scenic view of the beach, making it perfect for sunset dinners or relaxed weekend brunches.

The coastal décor is chic yet laid-back, with whitewashed furniture, tropical plants, and soft lighting that adds to its breezy vibe. Whether you’re on a date or catching up with friends, the space feels welcoming and Instagram-worthy.

Coming to the food — the menu is a fusion of global favorites and coastal classics. The seafood platter is a must-try, especially the butter garlic prawns and tandoori crab. Their wood-fired pizzas and mezze platters are great for sharing, and vegetarians won’t feel left out with ample flavorful options. The drinks menu offers a good mix of cocktails, mocktails, and fresh juices — the coconut mojito stands out as a refreshing hit.

Service is generally prompt and friendly, though it can get slightly slow during peak hours. Prices are on the higher side, but the quality of food and the ambiance justifies the spend.

Whether you're a local Mumbaikar or a tourist exploring Juhu, By The Bay is a great spot to unwind with good food and ocean views. The mocktails we had were Cinderella and Berry Blast. Both these were juice based drinks. Berry blast has Cranberry and Apple juice with a touch of honey.

For dessert we had a sizzling walnut brownie with ice cream. This was fresh and well made.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=a month ago, review=If you're looking for an unlimited affordable buffet in the Western Suburbs, Peshawari Grill in Goregaon East is a top Restaurant. Located on the 2nd floor of The Hub Mall, Western Express Highway, this Restaurant delivers a solid spread of veg & non-veg unlimited food in a comfortable, spacious setting.

From the moment we arrived, the ambience hit the right note — generous seating, warm lighting, and a relaxed vibe that works for both family dinners and friendly meet-ups. The staff are attentive and the buffet layout is well organised. They allow you to enjoy your dinner without disturbing much but be available when you call out any of them.

On to the food — you’ll find a wide variety of dishes: live counters with pani puri, soups, a full spread of starters (veg & non-veg kebabs, tandoori items), main courses ranging from North Indian to Chinese & Mughlai, breads, rice, and a nice dessert section.

Key favourites: the paneer tikka, chicken rarhya, lasooni fish, and for desserts the dudhi halw and kheer are worth a try.

With the special offer of ₹499 on Mondays & Tuesdays, you’re looking at an exceptional deal for the area.

The location is convenient for the Western Suburbs (Goregaon East), making it a solid choice for buffet restaurant in that region.

If I were to offer some tips:

Go early (lunch/dinner) to avoid peak crowd and ensure you get the full buffet spread without items running out.

Try out your best veg and non veg dishes - one at a time so that you don't get confused.
Start with the live counters (pani puri, kebabs) and work your way to mains & desserts — being strategic helps when you want to make the most of a buffet.

Bring your foodie group or family — the place has big seating which is great for group bookings.

In short: if you’re in Mumbai’s Western Suburbs and on the lookout for an unlimited food buffet restaurant that is within your budget, this is very much worth a visit. Paneer Chilly Samosa
Wontons

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Really well decorated restaurant, feels like a 5 star venue. Great service as well. Dal Makani was tasty while the tandoori chicken and naan was really good, bursting with flavours. The disappointment to me was the Gosht Biryani, the meat itself had a strange taste, I felt like it tasted a bit old. I made the visit to taste the handi style dish and was left a bit dissapointed. Still an overall good dining experience though., name_person=Dan Moodley}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=2 years ago, review=I went there on 16 April 23. For set menu dinner. They have very good options to choose for set menu like sea food / meat / veg / jain. We have taken 2 set menu 1 sea food and the other one was veg with rose wine.
Hospitality was amazing, and the food was too amazing. I could not finish the main course, just tasted and went to the desert, which was too yummy., name_person=Harsha Shah}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=7 years ago, review=One of the best dining place in Mumbai that offers authentic Indian food. Ambience was classy and you get a feel of nawabi tradition. Very friendly and respectful. Great Evening. The food was outstanding and the kulfi was to die for. Thank you for a great experience. The chef also gave us sampler for stuffed paneer and dal makhani which is very delicious. Amazing food, excellent service. Certainly visiting again., name_person=Food Search}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=I am glad that I visited this restaurant during my short stay in Mumbai. This is especially good for someone who has limited knowledge as to how to order food in India - this is my first meal after arriving the hotel at night. Excellent food (of course there are a few dishes that aren't that great but net-net I'm really satisfied) and good service/environment. Nice!, name_person=Raymond Li}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in}, time_line=3 years ago, review=‘Eat like a Nawab’. Nawab Saheb - The Westin Powai brings you a royal experience.
This place has a comfortable aura and interiors of this casual dining restaurant are appealing.
The cuisine is focused on traditional Indian featuring the regions of Awadh, Rajasthan and North West Frontier India. These flavours are influenced by local culture bringing out the authenticity to provide a world class gastronomic experience. The food is absolutely amazing – everything we tasted melted in other mouths especially GALAWAT KE KEBAB and LUCKNAWI GOSHT DUM BIRYANI. Absolutely the best meal we had
At Nawab Saheb you can enjoy culturally rich traditional dining experience which stays in your memory., name_person=Gargi Bagul}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Renaissance Hotel Powai is nothing short of royal and beautiful. Simply amazing hospitality and such pretty restaurants. This Infact, was my reason to visit Nawab Saheb for their ongoing Tawa & Tandoor Festival (20th- 28th September) as there are very few restaurants who actually go out of their way to curate special menus like these. Brainchild of Chef Yunus Khan, I think everything on the menu was fantastic. Service was slow as the restaurant was quite packed, being a Friday night. I opted for the vegetarian fare priced at 2800. Frankly, I thought it was value for money only because of the main course. Just their dal makhani and paneer will leave you licking your fingers till the end. Here's what the spread consisted of and how I felt about it :
Vegetarian :
1. Til Malai ka Phool (5/5)- Melt in the mouth brocolli with cream cheese. Found the cauliflower okayish.
2. Chef Yunus Khan ka Paneer Tikka (10/5)- Star dish! Has to be the best I've had in a long time. Highly recommended.
3. Subz ki Ashraphiya (3/5)- Found it average.
4. Bhune Bhutte ke Seekh (5/5)- AMAZING combination of seekh Kebab and babycorn. YUM.
5. Kabuki Kebab (3/5)- Found it too dry. Taste wise as well, bland due to Chickpeas.
6. Chukunder ke Kebab (4/5)- Beetroot galauti, it was nice.
7. Kumbh ke Galawat (5/5)- Wow. Has to be the one thing I'd come back for! Surprisingly it was served on a thepla kind of bread.
8. Aloo Atishi (4/5)- Bharwan aloo, classic.

Mains :
1. Paneer Kaliyan (10/5)- Now that's what I'm talking about. It's dishes like these that make you remember these hotels. No one does mains like them. I ALWAYS skip mains but yesterday I was too tempted after a bite and ended up having 3 pieces of bread after such heavy array of starters. MY FAVOURITE FROM YESTERDAY because it was cashew gravy, so creamy, soft paneer chunks and rightly spiced. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
2. Daal Nawab (10/5)- Probably as good as the one I've had in Delhi at ITC. Properly slow cooked for 48 hours, perfectly creamy and texture was just right. Not overdone. Yum.
3. Subz Biryani - couldn't dare to try it. Was too full.

Desserts : Assorted variety
Motichoor Laddoo, Kaju Katli, Kalakand, Gulab Jamun, Akhroti Halwa, Phirni - all were great but my favourites were the Phirni and Gulab Jamun.

Great staff and great hospitality by team. Special thanks to Manager Avanish, steward Shrikant and Chef Rahul Karve., name_person=Mahek Khanna}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=6 years ago, review=Nawab Saheb as the name suggests it’s a luxurious fine dine restaurant located in the basement of Renaissance Powai. This place was in my wish list since a very long time. I was amazed by the interiors and ambience of the place. The place can accommodate around 100 people at a time.

This place has maintained not just the standards but also taste of the food. The staff was very welcoming and warm with hospitality. Nawab Saheb is a gastronomical journey for those exploring the ageless Royal Mughlai and North Indian Cuisine.

The menu boasts of different menus such as Mix & Match, Seafood, Non-Vegetarian, Vegetarian and Jain options. Also, they have A-La-Carte menu. All these are eloquently curated by their Chef.

We started with Mix & Match Platter. The following dishes were adorned in the Platter.

Appetizers:

Nawabi Aloo Ki Nazakat

Chef Yunus Khan Ka Paneer

Dhuan Achari Lobster

Jheenga-e- Nisha

Akbari Murg Tikka

Shahi Gilawat Kebab

Mains:

Awadhi Paneer Korma

Makhamali Jheenga

Mahi Dum Qaliyan

Lagan Hara Murg

Potli Nihari

Dal Nawab Saheb

Gosht Awadhi Biryani

Desserts:

They have a dessert buffet in which you will get many Indian desserts. So, if you’re fan of Indian desserts it’s a perfect end to your meal.

Overall, a brilliant experience with the expertise in culinary world.

Food: 5/5

Ambience: 5/5

Décor: 5/5

Value for Money: 5/5

P.S: The review is strictly depending on my personal experience., name_person=shripad marathe}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=3 years ago, review=Nawab Sahab - Westin Powai
Amazing place , richness all over , menu curated by master Chef Yunus Khan a fusion of awadh , frontier India and Rajasthan
This place is known for it's Kebabs and mouth watering aromatic curries

Here is what we had :
==================

Veg and non veg platter - makai motiya seekh minced corn charred with Indian spices normally served on skewers. Since it was a platter it was a single piece
YONUS KHAN KA PANEER TIKKA - signature dish. Middle had a filling of dry fruits and nuts. Indian spices tandoor well with spices balanced
Subz gauloti - melt in mouth minced veggies with herbs and spices served over a bread. So Lucknow ( must try )
MALAI KA PHOOL - richness all over . Cheese and cream marinated broccoli charred.
Perfect

Non veg platter - Mahira babuli kebab famous dish of amritsar on bones. Melt in mouth tangy spicy marinating. Must try
GALAWAT KE KEBAB - do try this , served on a small paratha. Minced lamb with spices .balanced was prefect. Normally served on a griddle. Since it was a platter just had one piece which was enough to know the culinary talent of the master chef.

Samunder ki apsara - wow this was something new . Small lobster tandoor to perfection. Special spices used by the chef. I will remember this . Never had it as a starter

Coming to mains :
VEG - do try the Aminamadi  Saag , a spinach preparation with garlic and cumin. Freshly made full of flavours. Chef has kept it simple . Let the dish do the talking

Paneer Lazeez e khaas again a signature by chef. Chunks of cottage cheese with rich tomato gravy . Subtle in spices and aromatic at the same time.
However the 48 hour Long process Dal e yunus is worth a wait , rich urad lentil. Goes well with biryani or breads.

Non veg - ghost nihari tho banta hai boss . Bone marrow stock , lamb slowly cooked gives that aromatic taste and flavour.
Do try the murg handi lazeez - braised chicken with base of onion gravy along with methi ( fenugreek ) and cream. Chicken was cooked well tender and juicy

Must say that food , kebab or the gravy are not heavy or oily. Just perfect.
Missed out the prawns kasundi , lovely hit of kasundi cooked well. Velvety tomato and anar gravy. Do try.

Small portion of Subz Chilman biryani , long grain basmati rice with saffron a bit of Ittar ghee and veggies

Breads - Taftaan / Khameeri / Naan
However the dessert had a pleasant surprise
Had a capsicum halwa FOR the first time.
Something different which one needs to try out

Overall experience = awesome
Felt like a Nawab Dining at this place paired with a sparkling wine

Big thanks to Saurabh Dixit and team Westin for hosting

Ps. Only drawback , could not meet the master chef as had a day Off
Next time for sure
Till we meet again , cheers, name_person=Prithvish Ashar}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Good options to choose for set menu like sea food / meat / veg.}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=Delicious food, amazing sevice by the staff and soothing ambience}", "{person_name=null, guided_block={}, time_line=null, review=This is amazing .sea foods very tasty and yummy ...Good service..}"]

["{guided_block={}, time_line=a week ago, review=The outer-first-impression of Wasabi by Morimoto blends understated elegance and exclusivity: housed inside the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel (opposite Gateway of India), a short glass-and-steel lift or red-staircase transports you from the hotel lobby up to this refined Japanese dining space.  ￼
Guests seated near windows often enjoy partial views of the waterfront or Gateway, enhancing the ambiance.  ￼

Just loved each of them. Plus the view surely looks amazing.

Wonderful service Too., name_person=Prashant}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=5 years ago, review=First, yes it is expensive. Second, service is very good, attentive and knowledgeable. We liked most of the dishes except the salmon sushi which was just ok. The Yurine mousse was divine. A great experience., name_person=Saurabh Lal}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=8 years ago, review=My first real introduction to Japanese food. I am so glad we came here instead of going to my favourite Italian restaurant...
We had sushi and a sort of white asparagus (you can tell I am a total newbie) with a really delicious gravy.
A salad that the chef had made for the president of the US (I added mushrooms and it tasted Divine)... Am sure the president didn't get mushrooms with his salad.
They surprised us with a totally decadent rich dark chocolate cake with hints of raspberry in it. It was my birthday and this was a brilliant lunch.
We sat by the window and we should have had a view of the sea... But the building was undergoing construction so that was obscured.
The music was horrible and they did shut it off for a few minutes when we requested... But put it back on...
That was the only thing that spoilt a lovely afternoon out... But the food was so good, I couldn't give them a 4 star rating. It has to be a full 5!
Am I coming back here? Yes. Most definitely!, name_person=Khurshed Batliwala}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=Edited 2 years ago, review=One of the best Japanese restaurants in town although a little overpriced. Its a must try but only a once try kind of a restaurant. Except the rock shrimp tempura which wasn't that great in terms of taste none of the dishes justify their price when it comes to the portion or the lack of it. The king crab robatayaki was good but neither the the taste nor the portion justify the price. The dessert which again came recommended by the server was the highlight of the night. I would recommend going to the restaurant even if its just to try the dessert., name_person=Shubham Deshpande}", "{guided_block={}, time_line=2 years ago, review=Fantastic japanese cuisine with service to back it up. The chefs are well trained and masters at what they do as is evident by the presentation and detail. I would stay away from saucy dishes and just focus on the fish and rice and never be dissapointed here., name_person=Dan Moodley}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+}, time_line=3 years ago, review=After reading many good reviews and recommendations, we came to Wasabi with very high expectations, but the whole dinning experience was very disappointing, I suggest if you are Asian or foodie who has been to other countries and tried Japanese food, don't waste your money here.
We ordered 2 non-veg omasake, 2 soft beverages, 1 appetizer and 1 sushi, combination of omasake was a tragedy— heavy appetizers, everything was dipped in strong sauce, mayonnaise and Jalapeños on top, after thick starters they served light flavor nigiri sushi— your palate are already tired at this time, the mushroom rice and dessert are ok, but can't smooth our bad feeling, it’s the fusion Japanese cuisine that caters to foreigner taste, the whole dinner cost around INR 25,000, you will definitely have better options in Mumbai, especially Mumbai has bunch of fresh seafood can choose. Maybe because Wasabi is located in Taj Palace thus it’s so overpriced, but even more disappointed to have food of this quality under this shiny brand. This is peak Japanese food possible in India. Delighted to find sensible prices of wines on the Wasabi by Morimoto menu at Wasabi by Morimoto. I believe they have recently been rationalised, in keeping with the popularity of wine at the hotel and this restaurant, in particular. ["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[5-8_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_FIVE_TO_EIGHT], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=a month ago, review=Visited this on a Thursday evening for a group of 6 for Italian. After hearing mixed reviews regarding the food, we were quite unsure on what to expect, however, with high hopes, we still decided to visit.

Started off with their chicken tikka and the masala roomali roti. Didn’t disappoint. The chicken tikka was soft and very well seasoned. It was one of the very few I have had that doesn’t require the squeeze of lime to accentuate the taste. Paired with the roomali it was a started to get us started.

Moving on we had the butter naan along with the chicken tikka masala. Another stellar combo. Hot, fluffy naans with perfectly spiced chicken tikka masala with that perfectly caramelised onion flavour, something you should definitely order.

Next we moved to the chicken biryani. It’s a light biryani. Not too oily not too heavily reliant on array of spices. Simple yet tasty. Perfect lunch is what I would say.

Despite the reviews we managed to enjoy the food to our hearts content, name_person=Amol Surve}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Difficult to find parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_street_parking, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_STREET_PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=Up to 10 min, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION, Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION, Clearly_labeled_vegetarian_dishes, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_CLEARLY_LABELED_ITEMS]}, time_line=a month ago, review=Great restaurant. Beautifully designed and good service. The menu is a great Northern Indian journey. Quite sophisticated and not only your Indian classics. Good mix of Indian / Mogul cuisine. I had a chicken curry cooked to perfection as well as a great mutton masala kebab. Only thing: the waiter asked for tip a bit too pushy. I was happy with the service and would have given a generous tip anyway. But that was annoying., name_person=Christian Breitkreutz}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Moderate noise, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[2_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO, 3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=Average taste, great hospitality, interesting ambience.
Located at a prime spot, Khyber gives you the impression that it’s a classic where nothing can go wrong with the food. While it does not do anything wrong with the food, it also does not do anything marvellously well with it. The chicken kathi roll and the paneer tikka were so mildly marinated, one could barely get a sense of the spices used in the dishes. Even the cheese garlic naan was an average nibble.
The staff is warm and courteous., name_person=karman khanna}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=3 weeks ago, review=I tried a garlic Naan for the first time in Khyber back in 2015. I visited it for the second time in 2025 and I was as mesmerized as I was 10 years. But this time what stood out was the afghani chicken kebab. It was creamy, tender and so so flavourful. Would definitely recommend for a delightfully family Indian meal!, name_person=Anushka Pillai}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,800–2,000, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 months ago, review=We found Khyber through reviews, and it truly lived up to the hype. North Indian food never disappoints, and this place is a gem. The restaurant has a beautiful cave-like setting with warm vibes, and the servers were very polite.

We loved the chicken biryani – flavorful and aromatic – and the butter chicken was so creamy with perfectly tender chicken. Portions are decent and satisfying. Overall, if you’re looking for vibrant North Indian cuisine with great atmosphere, this is the place to go!, name_person=Anggie Puji}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Very quiet, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=3 months ago, review=The restaurant has a nice ambiance and the food was okay in taste. However, the service was quite slow and the food was not served hot, which affected the overall experience. With faster service and better attention to food quality, this place could be much better. Hoping to see improvements on my next visi, name_person=Mahesh Maurya}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=2 weeks ago, review=This was out first visit to this venerable Mughlai restaurant in Kalaghoda, in south Mumbai. The first thing that strikes you is the massive, ornate wooden door and once it swings open one can see the really beautiful archtecture of the restaurant featuring floating staircases and traditional furniture that is reminiscent of the northwest frontier though I noticed that the ceiling of the upper floor is extremely low.
I was tempted to compare Khyber to Punjab Grill, having visited the latter several times but Khyber now for the first time. Certainly the decor of Khyber is more earthy, more rural and yet more elegant. Punjab Grill now looks a little dated in some ways.
As for the food what I liked about Khyber was that the dishes were quite simple and the spices were mild and not overpowering. We sampled the corn tikkis, lamb rara and chicken tangdi. All were excellent and each dish was served separately as a course of its own. This was accompanied by naan and pudina paratha. For the three of us the bill came to less than Rs4,000, which was great value for money. Be warned, however, that this restaurant gets pretty busy and walk-in's could face a long wait though it's worth it, name_person=Indrajit Advani}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=4}, time_line=4 months ago, review=tried the Chicken Tikka, Chicken Butter, and Chicken Biryani — all were absolutely delicious! reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹600–800, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=4 weeks ago, review=​Hands down the best Japanese restaurant in Mumbai right now! I’ve tried many places across the city, but Donmai in Worli is on another level.
​We ordered a variety of dishes and the authentic taste really stood out. The Chicken Karaage was perfectly crispy and juicy, and the Salmon Sashimi was incredibly fresh—truly melt-in-the-mouth quality. You also have to try their Signature Sushi Rolls; the texture and balance of flavors were spot on.
​The vibe is a perfect mix of chill and upscale. If you are looking for top-tier, authentic Japanese food, this is the place. Highly recommended!, name_person=Rohit Sharma}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait}, time_line=2 months ago, review=The food was decent overall, though nothing particularly memorable. The *wasabi fries*, however, were quite off. The real standout was the *Kinoko Don pot rice*.. beautifully flavoured mushrooms and a really comforting, well-balanced dish. I didn't check the bar menu. If I had more appetite I would have definitely tried to find some cocktail in the cherry mocktail. Kareman was not on the menu as it will be launched for the next month menu. This was a veg option with egg or beacon as add on option. We had egg. The base of both the ramen were of oat milk which gives a flavour and texture similar to coconut milk with peanuts. We liked Kareman more than Chicken miso ramen. Japanese cheesecake was amazing. The space is spread over three floors, each with a distinct mood.\\n\u2022 Ground floor has al fresco seating (patio style), greenery, the entrance has terracotta pots, Jaisalmer stone jaali screens.\\n\u2022 First floor is more formal dining: yellow cement flooring, textured walls, sculptural wood furniture. Softer, more calming.\\n\u2022 Second floor / Bar area: moodier, more intimate. Deep hues (violet walls, etc.), vaulted ceilings, artistic murals (e.g. hand\u2011painted tiger motifs).\\nDetails of Rajasthani heritage show up subtly in decor: brass, stone, carved wood, warm earthy textures - feels lived\u2011in, comfortable.\\nThe cuisine is rooted in Indian regional flavours, especially coastal and Rajasthani. Desserts get creative - the Ghevar (Rajasthani dessert), Paan Magnum Kulfi etc. Nostalgic yet with some innovations. If you appreciate ambience, design, and wanting to explore awesome regional Indian cuisine with flair, it's a great pick. I tried their kerala chocolate ganache and it was served with a sorbet which made the dessert fantastic in taste.\\nThe food was good and the service was also quick and nice.\",\"guided_block\":{\"GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE\":\"Dinner\",\"GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE\":\"\u20b91,800\u20132,000\",\"GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT\":5,\"GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL\":\"Quiet, easy to talk\",\"GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE\":[\"2_people\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_TWO\",\"Suitable_for_all_group_sizes\",\"E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS\":\"Highly recommend\",\"GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO\":[\"Large_vegetarian_selection\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION\"],\"GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS\":[\"Vegetarian_options\",\"E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS\"]}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Nikita K\",\"time_line\":\"a month ago\",\"review\":\"\u201cHuman Jaha Pe Tameez Suey Khaya Hai, Bhuke Hi Wapas Aaye Hai\u201d\\n-A go-getter Foodie.\\n\\nIf luxury had a desi heart, it would look exactly like Joshi House. In the heart of Worli, this fine dining gem is a North Indian food lover\u2019s dream \u2014 blending authentic flavours with a refined modern touch. The ambience is simply stunning \u2014 warm lights, earthy d\u00e9cor, soft music, and an old-world charm that makes you want to stay longer. The perfect spot for an indulgent evening with friends, family, or even a quiet soulful date night.\\n\\nFor mocktails, we started with the Spice Sutra and the House Special J House. Both drinks were beautifully presented \u2014 vibrant, aromatic, and bursting with layered flavours.\\n\\nFor Appetisers,  we called for Sweet Potato Shammi Chaat which was an absolute delight! The soft shammi with the sweetness of potato, dash of ice-cold ice cream (Yes! Ice Cream) layer and tang from chutneys created a perfect harmony of flavours and Chutney Avocado Toast which was a creative twist on the classic! Creamy avocado topped with tangy Indian chutneys, giving every bite a fresh and fusion-style punch.\\n\\nThe bar was already set high by the appetisers, we were looking forward for the mains now. Next we ordered Beetroot Malai Kofta Curry which was smooth, and rich. The beetroot koftas were melt-in-the-mouth soft, perfectly paired with a luscious malai gravy. Enjoyed it with Cheese Garlic Naan, which was fluffy and indulgent and Paneer Tikka Biryani which was Fragrant, flavorful, and perfectly spiced. The tender paneer tikka chunks added that royal touch, making it a must-try for every biryani lover.\\n\\nAaaaand, for desserts we chose  Joshi House Ghevar \u2013 Our absolute favourite! A stunning dessert that truly stole the show. The presentation, the textures, and the sweetness \u2014 everything was on point. A perfect modern take on a traditional Rajasthani classic. Where was this all these years?\\n\\nJoshi House truly stands out not just for its food but for the complete experience it offers \u2014 from the elegant ambience to the impeccable service. A special thanks to Francis for the warm hospitality and for making our evening truly memorable.\\n\\nSuperb food, heart-touching flavours, and that Ghevar\u2026 ahhh still thinking about it!\",\"guided_block\":{}}", "{\"name_person\":\"Arhan Sarkar\",\"time_line\":\"2 years ago\",\"review\":\"4.0/5\\nJoshi House reminds me of a place where classical architecture meets modern art. The udon noodles were extremely tasty and were the second best item we tasted. Mind you, the noodles portion is large (for three, I'd guess). Next up, the Mexican Tacodillas-creamy, with a simple yet satisfying filling.
For mains, the Genovese Pizza stole the show with its perfect crunch and just the right touch of caramelized brown onions. Then came the 2 Cheese Ravioli, generously topped with basil pesto sauce-because, let's be honest, cheese + pesto is always a winning combo!

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,600–1,800, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=Edited 11 months ago, review=I recently visited Praia at the top floor of Atria Mall in Worli for the launch of the Cocktail Club and was absolutely taken by its vast, open-air ambiance. Spanning a generous 15,000 square feet, this rooftop eatery by restaurateurs Gaurav Dabrai and Kabir Luthria offers a laid-back vibe that’s perfect for watching the sunset—truly a luxury in the hustle of Mumbai.

The moment you step off the elevator and climb a short flight of steps, you’re greeted by soft amber skies (around 6 PM), friendly staff, and plenty of space to unwind. The seating includes cozy cabanas and tables under sail shades spaced far apart, giving the place an inviting, island-like feel. In fact, if you’ve experienced the nightlife in Greece, Praia’s atmosphere will remind you of the energetic bars in Mykonos.

One of the standout features is their dedication to live performances. There’s a stage set up for jazz dinners, supper theatre, weekend DJs, and more, ensuring a memorable dining and entertainment experience every time. Although they run only an evening service, Kabir points out that it was a deliberate choice to maintain a distinct nighttime charm at this location.

Whether you’re there to savor the scenic views, indulge in innovative cocktails (especially if you’re attending a launch like I did), or simply lounge under the stars, Praia has positioned itself as an unmissable spot in South Bombay’s dining scene. Palden norbu is cited at the rooftop of eskay resort in borivali.
Talking about the ambience it's simply stunning in all aspects. The open air seating looks really beautiful and the mix of white and blue color scheme looks fab. They also have few vibrant coloured swings which is a nice add on.

["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Lunch, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹800–1,000}, time_line=a month ago, review=⭐ 1/5 — Extremely Disappointing Experience at Landmark Restaurant, Dadar (Kohinoor Square)
We had one of the worst dining experiences at Landmark Restaurant, Dadar (Kohinoor Square). Our group of 13 people visited for lunch, and the staff suggested opting for their buffet at ₹650 per person. Unfortunately, everything from food quality to service was a complete letdown.
Service:
The service was painfully slow. We repeatedly had to request refills, and some of us were left waiting with empty plates for a long time. Even after several reminders, dishes arrived late and were poorly prepared. Despite it being a buffet, we constantly had to wait for food.
Food Quality:
The food was far below expectations.
Some dishes were extremely salty, while others had no salt at all.
The biryani was undercooked and tasteless.
The gulab jamun was raw in the center, and even after complaining, it wasn’t replaced.
The cheese balls were overly salty, and the overall spread lacked freshness and flavor.
Even the sweets — gulab jamun and kulfi — were of poor quality.
Staff & Management:
The staff seemed unprofessional and completely disinterested in resolving complaints. When we raised concerns, they just nodded and walked away without taking any action. The lady claiming to be the manager had no clue how to handle customers or address issues. It was obvious they cared only about payments, not about customer satisfaction.
Billing Issue:
To make matters worse, when it was time to pay, they charged ₹800 per person instead of the ₹650 initially quoted. When questioned, they blatantly denied ever mentioning ₹650 and refused to make any correction. We ended up paying ₹10,017 for substandard food and pathetic service.
Overall:

The lounge is located in the basement of Hotel Platinum so don’t get confused.

Surmai Fish

Perfectly cooked surmai with a crisp exterior and juicy, flaky flesh inside. Lightly spiced, fresh and lets the fish do all the talking.

Prawns Koliwada

Golden fried, crunchy on the outside and succulent within. Classic Koliwada masala that hits with spice and even tastier alongside the mint chutney.

Manchow Soup

Hot, hearty and comforting. Packed with chicken, veggies, bold Indo-Chinese flavours and that crispy noodles we all love.

Chicken Ghee Roast with Neer Dosa (Recommended)

A total show stealer. Fiery, rich ghee roast masala coating tender chicken, paired beautifully with soft, delicate neer dosas to balance it up.

Cold Coffee

Creamy, chilled and just the right amount of sweet.

Peach Iced Tea

Refreshing, fruity and light. Clean peach notes.

It was a delightful afternoon spent with great cocktails and surprising fusion of flavors and concepts. We were a party of six, so we could experience a lot on the menu and barring perhaps a couple of the dishes, every other dish was simply delectable and yum! There isn’t a “one” dish that I can single out as the highlight, there were multiple of them. Among the cocktails we tried:
·         Tamarind Whisky Shake – just a hint of the sweet sourness from the tamarind to add the kick but did not lose the character of the whisky
·         Waiting List – Gin based, curry leaf salt flavored, quite innovative in terms of the flavors
·         Stranger cocktail – Refreshing and again flavor packed
For drinks we also had the IPA, Belgian Wit and a green apple mocktail (green flag). The beers were nice but the mocktail was ok, especially compared to the bursts of flavors we were experiencing from the other drinks. A lot of what we ate was all simply superb and sent us down a flavor packed, surprise filled road! I mean – who would have thunk “kadi patta khakra” can taste that good!!! (that comes with the carrot thoran btw). The Chive brioche that came with the squid kheema pao was so amazing that we asked for two extra portions of just the brioche! Buttery, fluffy and heavenly! The dishes we ate and loved: Garlic Sourdough Naan, Morning Glory, Squid Kheema Pao, Mutton claypot rice, malai kofta, chur chur paratha, avocado papdi chaat, carrot thoran, seyal Pao (chef’s kiss!!!), and sea bass sev puri.

- Prawns Bhujane

Given the occasion, reservations were essential, and we were lucky to secure a table.

The ambiance was warm and cozy, with soft lighting and elegant décor that set the perfect romantic mood. The staff was incredibly attentive, ensuring we were comfortable throughout the evening. Their service was prompt, friendly, and efficient, adding to the overall delightful experience.

Now, let’s talk about the food—undoubtedly one of the best Italian restaurants in Mumbai! We began with some cocktails, which were decent, though not extraordinary. Moving on to the appetizers, we opted for the mushroom ravioli, and it was simply divine. The rich and creamy mushroom sauce paired perfectly with the stuffed chicken ravioli, creating a dish that literally melted in the mouth.

For the main course, we tried the Pollo Picante pizza. It had a bold, spicy kick that added a unique twist to the classic flavors. While it wasn’t the best pizza we’ve ever had, it was still delicious, with a perfectly crispy crust and generous toppings.

The real showstoppers of the evening were the desserts. The Tiramisu was, without a doubt, the best I’ve ever had—light, creamy, and full of rich coffee flavors. The chocolate goey cake was equally indulgent, with a soft center that was pure perfection.

The restaurant is spacious with ground and first floor seatings available and they have a bar too. The ambiance is really good with a nice Asian dine in feel created with plants and nice frames kept everywhere. Loved the seatings as it can accommodate all size of groups.

The menu contains pan asian dishes which means everything from sushi, Dimsums, Thai curry to Nasi Goreng, Khao Suey and more is available. Loved the menu as it provides great variety and honestly in that particular area no other restaurant has such a nice menu. The pricing is on point as the quantity served is huge.

Went here for a Sunday lunch and the kitchen service was on time. Thanks to staff Rylan as he made our table service smooth.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Volcano Maki Roll -
Fresh prawns with tempura crunch along with veggies tightly rolled with rice topped with spicy sauce tasted delicious. Loved the sushi as it was made perfectly.

Chicken Burnt Garlic Dumpling -
Thin outer covering and nicely filled with minced chicken tasted good. Didn’t felt much of burnt garlic in this however the overall filling tasted good.

Thai Chilli Basil Chicken -
This tasted outstanding. Juicy chicken with bell peppers tossed in spicy basil sauce was really good. The basil flavours along with garlic ginger was not too strong hence loved eating this.

MAINS~
Khao Suey -
Looked good and tasted heavenly. They serve the noodles and curry separately along with the condiments. Loved the flavours of the curry as it had nice amount of coconut milk plus spices used reduced the sweetness. The veggies and the chicken in the curry tasted great. A must try here.

Hakka Style Fried Rice -
A basic dish made perfectly which tasted good.

DESSERT~
Mango Sticky Rice -
This was from their limited time mango menu and trust me it was amazing. Sticky rice done in coconut milk served with alphonso mange was the perfect end to a perfect meal.

BEVERAGES~
Patong Passion.
Oriental Fuse.
Both the drinks tasted refreshing and went perfectly with the meal.

So our meal at Red Turtle Pan Asian Bistro was once again a treat as everything from ambiance, food to service was excellent. Christian Moreau Chablis 2016

It is very rare to find a Christian Moreau Chablis in India, and it was nice to see this wine on the menu at Le Cirque, Mumbai, and I ordered the same for my dinner.

Christian Moreau is one of the oldest and most respected domains in Chablis.
Wine has fruit notes like apple, green apple, pear etc.
A very beautiful and amazing Chablis wine.

Food Review:
A great wine needs great food.
That’s where the restaurant failed badly, and food was below average.

Initially their regular Chef prepared a dish based on lobster, and probably lobster was stale and the food was very bad which is not expected from such a restaurant.
Next a prawn based dish which was completely bad as well.
Finally I had a discussion with the restaurant manager and has concluded to change the regular Chef to another Chef Kamlesh to take over the dishes for dinner.
Kamlesh was comparatively better I felt when he prepared further dishes.

To be frank the restaurant had only me as a customer for the whole evening and it was very empty. Only one more customer came for a very short snacks that evening on another table.
I could understand it’s probably because of the bad Chef and lack of fine dining food menu.
I used to be a regular customer of the same restaurant Le Cirque in Bangalore which was much better as per my experience.

After discussing with Chef Kamlesh, I ordered smoked Scottish Salmon as starters which was very nice.
Followed by Pomfret dish which was quite average.
Next, another baked fish and vegetables.

Dessert:
The Chef Kamlesh suggested a portion of Crème Brûlée + Tiramisu.
Crème Brûlée was nice and tiramisu was average.

Conclusion:
To conclude, the overall experience was far below expectations.
The restaurant also didn’t had any special dishes like fish roe/caviar or scallops on the menu.
Food menu needs a lot of improvements to include fine dining dishes.
I could see that “Leela” failing very badly on expectations in Mumbai.

reviews:
["{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_RESERVATION=Reservations recommended, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3}, time_line=a month ago, review=It was not worth the hype, for a restaurant this famous with the kind of price they charge per person there was nothing unique, I'd ordered for a pizza but that did not end up coming to my table (the chef probably forgot it), the pasta was very basic, soups okok, the chatt counter was nice but that's something i can have anywhere, the inky love highlight for me was the cheese section nd Salads including the salami, main course as well was very okok (the goan prawns curry nd mutton was good) and lastly the dessert there were too many cake options and indian sweets which again I think I'd get at any other decent buffet (I grabbed the chocolate mouse, blueberry pie, cheesecake nd dark chocolate dessert), name_person=Michelle D'Souza}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=Edited 11 months ago, review=The ambience here is truly great and has always been a highlight 🌟. I’ve been visiting this restaurant 2-3 times a year for the last 5-7 years, and earlier, the taste they delivered was gold. Back then, they really tried to include everything in their buffet, and the dessert section used to be huge and impressive 🍰🍮.

Now, let’s talk about the breakfast buffet—it’s pretty standard, similar to what you’d find at any 5-star continental breakfast 🍳🥐. They do include a few Indian dishes, but honestly, breakfast here has never excited me since the beginning.

As for dinner, it used to be something I truly looked forward to because of how flavourful and varied the food was 🍽️. However, over the last 2-3 visits, it feels like something is always off—sometimes it’s the salt, sometimes it’s the flavours. The food feels same-same now, and perhaps I’ve become fed up of eating the same dishes repeatedly. There’s nothing new or exciting anymore, and the taste is not extraordinary enough to crave anything specific. I used to love the pizza here; it was one of my favorites. But lately, the taste has literally deteriorated 😞. It’s just not the same anymore, and it’s disappointing to see the quality drop. Hope they bring back the original flavors they were known for.

That said, this place still shines for its ambience ✨, and for newcomers, it might still feel impressive and worth the visit. But for me, my interest in visiting Lotus Cafe is slowly fading away 😕. I guess it’s a matter of having it too many times.

Still, for the overall experience, I’d rate it 4 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐., name_person=Ameen Shaikh}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_SEATING_TYPE=[Indoor_dining_area, E:DINING_SEATING_TYPE_INDOOR_DINING_AREA], GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹2,000+, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Loud, but you can still talk, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=4, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[Suitable_for_all_group_sizes, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_SUITABLE_FOR_ALL], GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=6 months ago, review=I visited this cafe a few weeks ago, for their famous Sunday brunch. I was spoilt for choice. They have a wide array of dishes to choose from.

I started off with their Asian dumplings and they were good. I absolutely loved chicken Sumai.

Next up, I tried a cheese platter with Gouda, Brie, burrata, cheddar, caramelised figs and crackers. Everything paired so well.

They had a wide range of cured meats, smoked tuna, smoked salmon and lots and lots of grilled veggies.

The lobster and oysters and tiger prawns were outstanding. Their mutton chops were delicious too.

But their pizza and drinks stole the show for me. The pizza base was perfectly chewy and charred while the cheese was melty and gooey. Their pineapple Pina colada was sweet and creamy.

The pasta was okayish. And some dish were just average.

They also had a wide range of dessert to choose from. But their Gulab Jamun and chocolate caramel dessert was overly sweet. But I loved their blueberry cupcake and chia seed pudding.

They added an unreasonably high service charge on both liquor and food (almost 40% extra). When we asked for clarification, instead of helping, the manager literally started shouting and arguing. Service was painfully slow and the staff seemed careless and completely untrained — no attention, no hospitality nothing, even basic requests were ignored multiple times.

Considering the prices they charge, the service and attitude are absolutely not worth it. There are many better clubs in the city where guests are treated with respect.

Overall, a terrible and stressful experience. Definitely not recommended.

The popular chef has left, and so have the quality & standards ...

A dinner on a fine day at this premium property was not destined to go well. Romano's, a restaurant which I had visited twice before, known for its close to flawless service & dishes, typical Italian style preparation and cuisine, and not to forget the sea bass, which was the best ever I had eaten anywhere in the same level hotels, but now it was all history. Today, the same restaurant had a below-average experience in stock for me.

Dishes took longer than the expected time. I had ordered a salmon and a sea bass and was told that it would take 20 and 25 mins respectively, but it took quite longer than that. While the salmon had a flaw, which upon complaining was first met with a response that it was good according to them, but they eventually agreed to replace it. Needless to say, taste buds do differ. Even on the second count, it didn't taste as it normally does. Surely not the first time I have tried it, and in fact, I have tried it in the same property a few times, and it was delicious previously, but this time, no offence intended, tasted weird. The quantity was too small, perhaps the smallest salmon I have eaten hitherto. This is highly likely because of the food festival discount which the restaurant offered. The second dish sea bass was not as good as last time, but still good enough. Again, the portion was quite small. The preparation was also different compared to last time.

The bread basket which is otherwise served, wasn't in this case ( I saw other customers getting one ). Again, this could be because I was availing a food festival offer. Even the mocktails took over 15 mins to be served, which is surprising, and instructions of less ice weren't followed. The blue mocktail was on a mild sweet and tangy side, and tasted good. The yellow one was average. The quantity of mocktails was medium. The restaurant was not too crowded either, so the wait time is indeed surprising.

Contrary to the case in the same level hotels, no one came to check in how the dishes were, and it was not easy to call the servers. The servers took a long time to come, and even when complained to someone in the coat ( I assume, a supervisor ), I was told sorry, but nothing changed. The supervisor didn't look much concerned about the experience and never came back to check if the concerns were resolved or not.

Attempts to resolve the concern at a senior level later ( since they weren't resolved in the restaurant properly ) went in vain. I was told that the issue would be looked into. However, my further messages were met with no response, which talks loudly about how much the senior level cares for the customers.

I wouldn't feel like going here again given their overall remiss approach. This wasn't even a four-star service. ["{guided_block={}, time_line=a month ago, review=We opted for buffet here and The primary positive point of our visit was the impressive variety and quality of the dishes offered on the buffet and the ambience. The kitchen staff clearly puts effort into preparation, offering a delightful mix of cuisines.

The Cheese Nuggets were a hit—crispy on the outside and warm/gooey inside. The Manchurian Dry was well-balanced and flavorful. Also, The inclusion of diverse items like Pasta, Khowswey, and various Dumplings was a pleasant surprise and added great value to the buffet. The taste of these dishes was genuinely good. The few Indian dishes available were noted for being flavorful and well-spiced, demonstrating skill across different culinary styles. Had the dining environment matched the quality of the food, this would have been a five-star review and a location we would frequent.

But, there are Major Cleanliness and Hygiene Failure
Unfortunately, the entire experience was severely compromised by unacceptable issues with cleanliness and hygiene in the dining and buffet area. The most critical issue was the pervasive presence of flies actively buzzing around and settling on the open food in the buffet line. This is a severe health and safety risk. Due to the sight of pests, we were forced to avoid several dishes entirely, including many we were looking forward to trying. This lack of sanitation completely overshadowed the good food, making the meal stressful and unappetizing. A buffet setup requires rigorous and constant attention to hygiene. If there’s a global award for “How Not to Run a Club,” Mitron would win by a landslide. Let me break down this disaster of an experience:

💸 Cover Charge Robbery: They charged an obscene cover at the entrance, promising a “premium experience.” What they delivered was the exact opposite of premium—think overpriced chaos with zero value. Spoiler: thanks to delays and drama, no one could even finish the amount we’d already paid cover for.

👥 Crowd Density: Imagine cramming three busloads of people into a broom closet. That’s the vibe. You can’t move, can’t breathe, can’t even lift your hand to sip your drink. Fire safety clearly never crossed management’s mind.

🍹 Drinks & Food Service: If you’re into waiting 45 minutes for a watered-down cocktail and another hour for soggy finger food, this is your paradise. The bar staff moved slower than dial-up internet, and the kitchen seemed to be on strike.

🎶 Music Quality: Calling it music is generous. The DJ seemed to be experimenting with broken YouTube playlists—random transitions, distorted speakers, and bass so bad it rattled your bones but not in a good way. Forget dancing, you’ll be too busy cringing.

🚨 Grand Finale: Police Raid: Just when people thought it couldn’t get worse—surprise! Police stormed the place. Lights on, music cut, everyone herded out like cattle. And here’s the kicker: because of the insane delays in serving, we hadn’t even used up their exorbitant cover charge. Basically, we paid for the privilege of standing in a sweaty, overcrowded box before being kicked out early.

👎 Overall: A masterclass in how to ruin a night out. Unjust cover charges, suffocating crowd, incompetent service, awful music, and the cherry on top—a raid. The only thing intoxicating here is the sheer incompetence.

Final verdict: If you want to burn your money while being miserable, this is the place. Otherwise, avoid like the plague.

We had booked our   buffet through zomato with 50 % discount. It was full Paisa vasool  for the price we paid ( ₹3000 after discount for 2 pax ).

The buffet spread was not vast even on Sunday. But it was decent enough. Since I am a vegetarian, I didn't saw the non veg options but there were  seperate counters for salad, chat ( pani puri, sev puri and dahi Puri ), live counter ( veg pasta ), soup ( 1 veg and 1 non veg ), sweets ( gulab jamun + brownie fudge ), indian main course ( 3 veg + 3 non veg sabji ), fried rice + manchurian, biryani ( veg + non veg ) and a dessert counter with 5 veg and 3 non veg desserts. The only thing was missing were non alcoholic drinks ( mocktails ) which should be included in the menu.
Mr. Amit and Mr. Nilambari ( sorry if wrongly spelled ) were very attentive and comforted us in every possible way.

Overall we had a nice time together with superb food and service made our day., name_person=Hitesh Jain}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Highly recommend, GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Breakfast, GUIDED_DINING_DISH_RECOMMENDATION=[Tiramisu], GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Dietary_restrictions, E:OTHER_DIETARY_RESTRICTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Menu_is_all_vegetarian, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_COMPLETELY_VEGETARIAN, Large_vegetarian_selection, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_LARGE_SELECTION]}, time_line=8 months ago, review=Excellent staff. Very polite and very helpful. Love the environment and vibes. The outdoor garden area is 5/5.

I personally would prefer to have more non veg options other than chicken., name_person=mohamed sammaan}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=1, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=2}, time_line=a year ago, review=I am staying at the hotel at the moment and I had a buffet dinner tonight at the Fiona restaurant which was one of the worst Indian buffets I ever encountered in my life anywhere in the world let alone in a 5 star hotel.
And to think this is in Mumbai, India 🇮🇳 (oh, the irony).

Upon arrival I was asked if I wanted still or sparkling water.

I opted for sparkling water.

It is perrier, a French mineral water which is fairly priced at 300 inr + + (comes to around 3.90 EUR which is the same as what a small mineral water in a 5 star hotel in France typically costs).

However, perrier spent a quarter of a billion EUR recalling and destroying millions of mineral water bottles this year because it admitted one of its seven water wells in Southern France had fecal contamination due to heavy flooding.

It would be better had I been told what exactly I was getting rather than "sparkling water".

As it is a small bottle I decided to drink it but I can't for the life of me understand why a buffet restaurant can't have a drinks menu.

I started with pani puri and dahi puri which were the only tasty items.

After being seated I was not asked if I want any bread to accompany the meal.

It is only after I got my food that I realised it must be ordered so the bread arrived after my food was already sitting for a while.

The waiter said they have "all Indian breads".
I asked for a kulcha and a roti.
I got a plain naan and a roti instead and both tasted below average.

In order not to write a long essay I will suffice by saying that the non-veg food is so bad I would not opt to purchase the meat if on display in a chicken or mutton shop I frequent when feeding the dozens of stray dogs on my visits to India..

Everything (with the exception of the chaat/pani puri) was extremely salty and in fact non edible.

The salads uninspiring (i.e a thick slice of boiled beetroot stuck between some other bits and pieces, a bowl of dry lettuce with no sauce whatsoever etc.)

The so called biryani and the paneer swimming in cheap oil were so salty I couldn't eat them and returned the plate to the waiter.

The same was true for the so-called "hara bhara kebab".
It was a dry salty patty and had nothing in common with hara bhara as I know and love.

The sweets were edible but not particularly tasty either.

After this experience I will surely not try the buffet breakfast tomorrow nor for the rest of my stay which is otherwise very pleasant., name_person=Budmil Budapest}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_TIPS_TOPICS=[Vegetarian_options, E:VEGETARIAN_OPTIONS, Parking, E:PARKING, Kid-friendliness, E:KID_FRIENDLINESS], GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_SPACE_AVAILABILITY=Plenty of parking, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=2, GUIDED_DINING_RECOMMEND_TO_VEGETARIANS=Somewhat recommend, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,200–1,400, GUIDED_DINING_NOISE_LEVEL=Quiet, easy to talk, GUIDED_DINING_PARKING_OPTIONS=[Free_parking_lot, E:PARKING_OPTION_FREE_PARKING_LOT], GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=3, GUIDED_DINING_GROUP_SIZE=[3-4_people, E:DINING_GROUP_SIZE_THREE_TO_FOUR], GUIDED_DINING_WAIT_TIME=No wait, GUIDED_DINING_VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO=[Vegetarian_menu_or_section, E:VEGETARIAN_OFFERINGS_INFO_SEPARATE_MENU_SECTION]}, time_line=7 months ago, review=I would never suggest anyone for having buffet lunch/dinner here.
